name: ContinuousValueGradient window spans tau + 3*dt, not tau
location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:59-61
claimed_object: The state of the delay differential equation is the path x_t on EXACTLY [-tau, 0]. Its discretisation on the control grid is ceil(tau/dt)+1 taps spanning exactly tau, which is precisely what the environment's own integrator buffer holds (env_rk_jax.py:30-31, measured span == tau to 1e-9 in every delayed cell).
actual_behaviour: `_compute_window_size` returns `int(np.ceil(max_delay / self.env.step_size)) + 3 if max_delay > 0 else 10`. With window_length = window_size + 1, the window carries exactly 3 taps strictly older than -tau. MEASURED spans (x64 on, as main_unified.py:63 sets): linear_dde_scalar 1.6000 vs tau=1.0; platoon_h1h2 0.3500 vs tau=0.2; MG_1D_limit_cycle 6.7500 vs tau=6.0; MG_1D_chaotic 17.7500 vs tau=17.0; hopfield_linear/nonlinear/duffing 0.8000 vs tau=0.5. fires_in_practice: MEASURED on linear_dde_scalar (value_gradient, x0=0.5): per-tap ||dV/dx(tap)|| gives ||dV/d(taps at t < -tau)|| / ||dV/d(taps in [-tau,0])|| = 0.3074 at initialisation and 0.1921 after 20 training episodes. The value functional is therefore demonstrably NOT a function of x_t alone: it responds to x(-1.6), x(-1.4), x(-1.2), which are not part of the state. logged: No. The window is derived silently — ContinuousValueGradient prints nothing at all when it overrides the configured window_size, and nothing states the span or the excess.
recommendation: Return `int(np.ceil(max_delay / self.env.step_size))` so window_length = window_size + 1 spans exactly tau. If a margin is ever genuinely required (e.g. to guard interpolation at the delayed lookup), it must be justified in a comment, be at most the interpolation stencil width, and be reported in the run log alongside the resulting span versus tau. Re-measure the excess-tap sensitivity ratio after the change; it must be identically zero because the taps no longer exist.

name: The taps outside [-tau, 0] are fabricated at reset by constant front-padding
location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:160-171 (and the mirrored fill in src/agents/signatures_jax.py:270-280)
claimed_object: The initial condition of the delay differential equation is the path phi in C([-tau,0], R^d), and nothing else: the plant is simply not defined before -tau.
actual_behaviour: `wrapper.initial_conditions` returns exactly the environment's buffer, which spans exactly tau; subsampled to the control cadence it yields ceil(tau/dt)+1 taps. The agent's window needs 3 (value gradient) or 1 (signatures) MORE taps than that, so the `else` branch front-pads with `subsampled[0]`, i.e. it invents a constant extension of phi to the left of phi's own support. MEASURED front-pad counts at reset: linear_dde_scalar 3 (value gradient) / 1 (signatures); hopfield_linear 3 / 1; MG_1D_limit_cycle 3 / 1; platoon_h1h2 3 / 1; double_integrator 10 / 10 (of 11 taps — the env supplies exactly 1 usable tap). At t=0 the critic therefore evaluates V on a path the plant never followed. Once the episode advances past the pad, those slots fill with genuine trajectory — but genuine trajectory OLDER than tau, which is still not part of x_t.
fires_in_practice: MEASURED: the pad executes on every reset of every cell (counts above). Its numerical effect is masked in the shipped configs only because `fix_initial_state: true` makes phi constant, so the constant extension agrees with phi's own value; with a non-constant `history_function` the padded window opens on a path with a spurious flat segment. The downstream effect is measured and non-zero regardless (excess-tap sensitivity ratio 0.19-0.31 on linear_dde_scalar).
logged: No. The pad is silent — no count, no warning, no record that the window contains invented data.
recommendation: This finding dissolves once the window spans exactly tau: the subsampled history then has exactly the required length and the pad branch becomes unreachable. Keep the branch as a guard, but make it raise (or warn-once with the count and the times of the fabricated taps) rather than silently invent data, so that any future (tau, dt, resolution) that under-supplies the window announces itself.

name: The origin_augmentation basepoint is read from a tap outside the state
location: src/utils/dynamic_signature.py:199-203 (data[0]) fed by the over-long window from src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:59-61
claimed_object: The Perez Arribas (2018) basepoint channel injects X_0, the level at the START of the window. If the window is the state x_t on [-tau,0], then X_0 = phi(-tau) = x(t-tau), which is a genuine coordinate of the state.
actual_behaviour: The ramp channel is built as `origin = data[0] * elapsed_fraction`, so it injects `data[0]` = the OLDEST tap. Because the window is over-long, data[0] sits at t-tau-3*dt (value gradient) or t-tau-dt (signatures), NOT at t-tau. The injected 'absolute level' is therefore the level of a point outside the state; and at reset that point is a FABRICATED pad value (previous finding), so the basepoint channel at t=0 is built from invented data.
fires_in_practice: MEASURED on linear_dde_scalar: the per-tap value-gradient profile is [0.005, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0.016] at init and [0.002, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0.011] after 20 episodes — the sensitivity is concentrated ENTIRELY on tap 0 (the basepoint, at t=-1.6) and the endpoint tap. Tap 0 is the single largest non-endpoint contributor to V, and it is outside [-tau,0]. This is the mechanism by which the over-long window binds.
logged: No.
recommendation: Correcting the window span to exactly tau fixes this automatically: data[0] then lands on phi(-tau) = x(t-tau), a true state coordinate. Add a comment at dynamic_signature.py:199 recording that data[0] is REQUIRED to be x(t-tau) and that this holds only if the window spans exactly tau, so the invariant is stated where it is consumed. Note separately that origin_augmentation has already been shown this session to break Chen's identity for the sliding window (residual 1.14); that is a distinct defect and is not addressed by the span fix.

name: Subsampling anchors on the oldest sample, so the window endpoint is not guaranteed to be x(t)
location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:158 and src/agents/signatures_jax.py:276 — `subsampled = history_data[::self.env.resolution]`
claimed_object: The window's LAST tap must be the endpoint x(t): the Doya greedy law u* = -(1/2) R^{-1} g(x_t)^T grad_{x(t)} V is Dupire's VERTICAL derivative, i.e. the derivative with respect to the window's endpoint. `_make_action_jit_fn` implements this as `end_gradient = grad_path[-1]` (value_gradient_jax.py:196-197), which is correct only if grad_path[-1] is the gradient at x(t).
actual_behaviour: `history_data[::resolution]` strides from index 0 — the OLDEST tap — so it retains the newest sample only when (buffer_size - 1) is divisible by resolution, i.e. only when tau/dt is an integer. Otherwise the newest sample is dropped and the window's last tap is a stale state; `grad_path[-1]` is then the vertical derivative at the WRONG point, and the control law is evaluated off the endpoint. The correct stride anchors on the newest sample (`history_data[::-1][::resolution][::-1]`).
fires_in_practice: MEASURED, latent for the shipped delayed cells but live in general. On linear_dde_scalar as shipped (tau=1.0, dt=0.2, res=4, tau/dt=5 integer) the retained times are [-1.0, -0.8, -0.6, -0.4, -0.2, 0.0] and the endpoint IS x(t) — inert. With delay overridden to 0.3 (tau/dt = 1.5, non-integer) the retained times measured [-0.3, -0.1]: the newest sample at t=0 is DROPPED and the window endpoint holds x(-0.1) while the true x(t) = 0.0 — measured 'ENDPOINT IS *NOT* x(t)'. On double_integrator as shipped the subsampling measured a single retained tap at t=-0.025, not t=0, so the endpoint is x(-0.025); this is numerically inert ONLY because fix_initial_state makes phi constant. Every currently shipped delayed cell has integer tau/dt, so the defect does not bind on present results — it binds silently the first time a non-commensurate tau is used.
logged: No. There is no assertion that the retained endpoint time is t, and no warning when the stride drops it.
recommendation: Anchor the stride on the newest sample rather than the oldest, and add a hard assertion at the fill site that the retained endpoint time equals the current time to within 1e-9 (the times are already available from `wrapper.initial_conditions`). This is cheap, executes once per reset, and converts a silent wrong-object failure into an immediate abort. Add a regression test with a non-integer tau/dt (e.g. tau=0.3, dt=0.2) — the present test suite cannot catch this because every fixture uses commensurate values.

name: float32 narrowing of the initial path phi in a float64 window
location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:163, 168, 171 — `np.asarray(x/self.training.scale, dtype=np.float32)`
claimed_object: The window is a float64 object end-to-end: `RepresentationBuffer` is constructed with `dtype=np.float64` (factory.py:66), `DequeBuffer.to_array` casts to float64, and main_unified.py:63 enables jax_enable_x64. phi should enter the window at the pipeline's working precision.
actual_behaviour: `_fill_buffer_initial` bypasses `RepresentationBuffer.append` (which correctly casts to the buffer's float64 dtype) and writes straight into the raw deque with an explicit `dtype=np.float32`. `to_array()` then upcasts the ALREADY-rounded value back to float64, so the loss is irreversible and invisible in the reported dtype. Every subsequent tap enters via `update_buffer` -> `append` at float64 (value_gradient_jax.py:449-450), so the window is INHOMOGENEOUS in precision: the initial-path taps carry ~8 significant digits, the evolving taps ~16.
fires_in_practice: MEASURED on linear_dde_scalar with x0 = 1/3: the env history value is 0.3333333333333333, the value stored in the window is 0.3333333432674408 — absolute round-off 9.934e-09, RELATIVE 2.980e-08, i.e. roughly 1.3e8 times the float64 eps (2.220e-16). `agent.sliding_signature.buffer.dtype` reports float64, which conceals the loss. It fires on every reset of every cell whenever x0 is not a dyadic rational; it is inert for x0 = 0.5 or 1.0 (the shipped eval defaults), which is why it has survived.
logged: No — worse than unlogged, the reported buffer dtype (float64) actively contradicts the stored precision.
recommendation: Route the fill through `self.sliding_signature.append(...)`, exactly as `update_buffer` does and as signatures_jax.py:281 already does. This is the residual of code-review finding F-E1 (commits 07b8d4a / 7b1153e moved the buffers to float64 and missed this path); the signatures_jax._fill_buffer_initial docstring already names it as a known outstanding defect in the sibling agent. Add a test asserting the window round-trips x0 = 1/3 to float64 eps.

name: force_signature_window semantics are inverted relative to its documentation and its own log line
location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:56-57; src/agents/signatures_jax.py:164-167; conf/agent/value_gradient.yaml (`force_signature_window: false  # if true, override window_size to match max delay`)
claimed_object: A configuration flag and its log line must describe what the code does, since they are the only record a reader has of which window was used.
actual_behaviour: The code reads `if not self.signature_conf.force_signature_window: self.signature_conf.window_size = <derived from delay>`. So force_signature_window=FALSE is what overrides the window to match the delay, and TRUE keeps the user's raw yaml value. Both the yaml comment ('if true, override window_size to match max delay') and the log line assert the opposite. The log line printed in the True branch is `f"force_signature_window is True: setting window_size to {window_size} to cover max delay of {max_delay}"` — in that branch nothing is set, and the claim of covering the delay is false.
fires_in_practice: MEASURED on linear_dde_scalar (tau=1.0, dt=0.2, yaml window_size=40): with force_signature_window=false the used window_size is 8 (value gradient) / 6 (signatures) — the flag being FALSE is what forced the window from the delay. With force_signature_window=true the used window_size is 40 for both, and the signatures agent printed verbatim `force_signature_window is True: setting window_size to 40 to cover max delay of 1.0` — measurably false on both counts: it set nothing, and 40 taps at dt=0.2 spans 8.0 s against tau = 1.0 s, an 8x over-coverage.
logged: Yes, but the log is FALSE, which is worse than silence: a reader who trusts it concludes the window covers tau when it covers 8*tau.
recommendation: Rename the flag to state what it does (e.g. `window_size_from_configuration`, default false) or invert the test to match the documented meaning; correct the yaml comment; and replace the log line with the measured facts — the resolved window_size, the resulting physical span window_size*step_size, tau, and their difference — printed unconditionally on BOTH branches by both agents.

name: The resolved window is never persisted: every run's config.yaml records a window that was not used
location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:56-57 and src/agents/signatures_jax.py:164-165 (mutate the dataclass, not cfg) versus main_unified.py:331 (`(run_dir / "config.yaml").write_text(OmegaConf.to_yaml(cfg))`)

location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:61 (`... else 10`) and src/agents/signatures_jax.py:163 (`... else 10`)

name: The window clock is dimensionless and time_origin is a dead parameter
location: src/configs.py:86 (`time_origin: float = 1.0`); src/representations/factory.py:41-47 and src/representations/signature.py:33-42 (never forward it); src/utils/dynamic_signature.py:206 (`jnp.linspace(0.0, time_origin, n)`)
claimed_object: The state is a path parametrised by physical time s in [-tau, 0]. The monotone time channel of the Perez Arribas augmentation is what makes the signature injective on the augmented path.
actual_behaviour: `SignatureConfig.time_origin` is defined but neither `make_representation` nor `SignatureRepresentation.__init__` forwards it to `SlidingSignatureJAX`, so the default 1.0 always applies and the time channel is `linspace(0.0, 1.0, n)` — a per-window normalised clock. The physical span is therefore NOT encoded: a window spanning tau and one spanning tau + 3*dt produce identical time channels, and windows from cells with different (tau, dt) are parametrised identically. The docstring at dynamic_signature.py:190-195 states the normalisation and argues the rescale is absorbed by the downstream layer — that argument is exact for the depth-1 terms but not for the mixed higher-depth terms, which scale with different powers of the channel.
fires_in_practice: MEASURED as dead: `grep -rn time_origin` over the repository finds no config file setting it and no call site forwarding it, so dynamic_signature.py:206 always receives 1.0. The normalisation is a FIXED reparametrisation within any single run (the window length is constant), so it does not change that run's answer — hence classification D rather than B. Its cost is that the physical span is absent from the features, so signature values are not comparable across runs with different spans, and the +3 / +1 excess is invisible to the feature map. The magnitude of any cross-run effect is NOT MEASURED.
logged: Not applicable — no runtime clamp; the issue is a dead parameter and a missing physical scale.
recommendation: Remove `time_origin` from SignatureConfig, or forward it and set it to the window's physical span (window_size * step_size) so the clock is in seconds and the augmented path is the actual path on [-tau, 0]. State the choice in the docstring alongside the existing normalisation argument, and note explicitly that the absorption argument covers the depth-1 terms only. Lowest priority of this set: it does not corrupt any current number, unlike the span, endpoint, and provenance findings above.

name: The value-gradient control law is the CARE control (decisive test PASSES at scale = 1)
location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:203
claimed_object: u* = -(1/2) R^{-1} g(x_t)^T grad_{x(t)} V(x_t). With the plant's reward convention r = -(x^T Q x + u^T R u) (env_rk_jax.py:88, reward is MAXIMISED), the Doya Hamiltonian H(u) = -x^T Q x - u^T R u + (grad_x V)^T B u is stationary at u = +(1/2) R^{-1} B^T grad_x V. The PLUS sign and the factor 1/2 are therefore both correct for this reward convention.
actual_behaviour: `u = 1/2*jnp.linalg.inv(R) @ B.T @ end_gradient` with `end_gradient = grad_path[-1]`. MEASURED against scipy.linalg.solve_continuous_are on conf/env/double_integrator.yaml (A = [[0,1],[0,0]], B = [[0],[1]], Q = I, R = [[1]]), with the markovian degree-2 critic kernel set analytically so that V(x) = -x^T P x exactly (verified: V_code = -3.1650635095 against -x^T P x = -3.1650635095). Control comparison at three states: x = (1, 0.5) -> u_code = -1.8660254, u_CARE = -1.8660254, ratio 1.0; x = (-2, 3) -> u_code = -3.19615242, u_CARE = -3.19615242, ratio 1.0; x = (0.3, -0.7) -> ratio 0.99999996 (the 4e-8 residual is the separate float32 fill finding). Endpoint identity separately MEASURED on hopfield_nonlinear over 12 mid-episode steps: max |window[-1] - x(t)| = 1.192e-08 (attained only at step 0, from the float32 fill; exactly 0.0 at every subsequent step), so grad_path[-1] IS the derivative with respect to the window endpoint and not with respect to a stale buffer sample. The subsampling alignment was checked across all 14 delayed env configs: the last subsampled tap coincides with the newest env-buffer entry in every one. Autodiff grad_path[-1] agrees with a central difference in window[-1] to 4.986e-11.
fires_in_practice: MEASURED: exact agreement with the CARE control on the double integrator at scale = 1.0 (ratio 1.0 to float64 precision at exactly-representable states). The paper's reported sign error is NOT present in the code.
logged: n/a — no device; this item records the verification.
recommendation: No change. Add a one-line comment at line 203 stating the reward convention that fixes the sign (r = -(x^T Q x + u^T R u), maximised), since the sign is only correct relative to that convention and the paper disagrees. Consider promoting the CARE comparison above into test/agents/ as a regression test — it is a two-line assertion that pins the sign, the factor 1/2, and the endpoint alignment simultaneously.

name: training.scale is missing the 1/scale chain-rule factor in the control law
location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:203 (with the scaling introduced at :163, :171, :336, :346, :450, :691)
claimed_object: The critic consumes the scaled window z = x/scale, so it represents V~(z) = V(x) with x = scale*z. The chain rule gives grad_x V(x) = (1/scale) * grad_z V~(z). The control law therefore requires u* = (1/2) R^{-1} B^T * (1/scale) * grad_path[-1].
actual_behaviour: `end_gradient = grad_path[-1]` is grad_z V~, i.e. scale * grad_x V, and is fed to the control law with NO 1/scale correction. The implemented control is scale * u*. MEASURED on double_integrator with scale = 4.0 and the critic kernel re-fitted so that the represented value is exactly the true-unit V(x) = -x^T P x (verified: V_code = -3.165064 against -3.165064, and -10.516660 against -10.516660 — the value itself is correct, only its gradient is mis-transported): x = (1, 0.5) -> u_code = -7.46410162 vs u_CARE = -1.8660254, ratio exactly 4.0; x = (-2, 3) -> u_code = -12.78460969 vs u_CARE = -3.19615242, ratio exactly 4.0. The reward (env_rk_jax.py:88) and hence the reported cost are in TRUE units, so the learned object is the value of the true plant, mis-transported into a control that is inflated by exactly the factor scale. Closed-loop cost penalty of the inflated gain, MEASURED by integrating the double integrator from x0 = (1, 0.5) over [0, 40] at rtol = 1e-10: scale = 1 -> J = 3.165064 (optimal, = x0^T P x0); scale = 2 -> J = 3.685696 (+16.45%); scale = 4 -> J = 5.467317 (+72.74%); scale = 10 -> J = 11.365490 (+259.09%); scale = 50 -> J = 51.503189 (+1527.24%).

name: The representation window spans tau + 3*dt, not [-tau, 0]

name: divergence_threshold silently truncates the objective integral

claimed_object: J = integral over [0, T] of the discounted running reward r(x(t), u(t)). Every episode's reported cost must be the same functional over the same horizon T = training.max_time.
actual_behaviour: The episode terminates the moment ||x|| exceeds the bound, and `episode_cost` (line 525) is then the integral over [0, T'] with T' < T. The reported series therefore mixes an integral over 5.30 s with integrals over 15.00 s with no marker distinguishing them. Because the reward is strictly negative (env_rk_jax.py:88, r = -(x^T Q x + u^T R u) <= 0), truncation always removes negative mass: a cut episode's cost is biased UPWARD relative to the functional it claims to report, i.e. the cut systematically flatters the very episodes that are diverging. (In the measured run the cut episode still reports the worst cost, because it was diverging hard enough that 5.3 s of divergence outweighed 15 s of a merely bad policy — the bias is present but was not large enough to invert the ranking on this particular run.)
fires_in_practice: MEASURED. DOES fire under stress: 1 cut in 12 episodes and 1 cut in 60 episodes at x0 = 10*ones with critic_lr = 1.0, std_init = 1.0. Summary: the bound sits roughly two orders of magnitude above the state norms reached at the settings actually used, so it is not currently contaminating any reported number — but that is a measured property of the current settings, not a property of the code, and it is invisible if it changes.
logged: No. `_is_episode_done` returns True in silence. Nothing in the metrics, the progress bar, or the run log records that an episode was cut, how many were cut, at what time, or how far past the bound the state went. A reader of `cost_episodic` cannot tell truncated points from complete ones. This is a direct violation of the project rule: a clamp that can alter a reported number must report when it binds.
recommendation: (i) Log the first activation at WARNING and subsequent ones at DEBUG, recording the episode, the cut time t, the horizon T, and the pre-cut ||x|| (per the project's warn-once helper convention). (ii) Record a per-episode `truncated: bool` and `horizon_actual: float` in metrics_history, and either exclude truncated episodes from the cost curve or mark them distinctly — never plot two different functionals as one series. severity: medium (silent; measured not to fire at present settings, so no current number is contaminated — but unlogged, and it biases the metric in the direction that hides divergence)

name: clip_action is silent, and is the box-constrained argmax only because every shipped R is diagonal
location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:204-205 (`if do_clip: u = jnp.clip(u, -clip_action, clip_action)`)
claimed_object: u* = argmax over u in R^m of the Doya Hamiltonian H(u) = -x^T Q x - u^T R u + (grad_x V)^T B u. A clipped control is a different control; the honest question is whether it is the argmax of the same Hamiltonian over the box {u : |u_i| <= c}.
actual_behaviour: The unconstrained argmax is clipped coordinate-wise. ANSWER TO THE ARGMAX QUESTION, established numerically: H is concave in u with Hessian -2R. For DIAGONAL R the objective separates across coordinates, so the box-constrained argmax IS the coordinate-wise clip of the unconstrained one — MEASURED over 200 random draws of w = B^T grad_x V ~ N(0, 8^2 I) with R = diag(1, 2), c = 1: max |clip(u*) - argmax_box H| = 2.468e-08 (L-BFGS-B, 12 restarts; residual is optimiser tolerance). For NON-DIAGONAL R the objective does not separate and the clip is NOT the box-constrained argmax — same protocol with R = [[1, 0.8], [0.8, 1]]: max |clip(u*) - argmax_box H| = 2.000e+00, i.e. the full width of the box. Every R inspected across conf/env/*.yaml is diagonal or scalar ([[1.0]], [[0.1]], numpy.eye, and chemical_reaction_4D's [[0.1, 0.0], ...]), so the clipped control currently IS a well-defined greedy control — of the box-constrained problem, which is a DIFFERENT optimal control problem from the one the objective states, with a different value function and a different Riccati/HJB solution. The code does not say this anywhere, and the property is one non-diagonal R away from being false, at which point the control is the argmax of nothing.
fires_in_practice: MEASURED. Never binds in the value-gradient agent as shipped: conf/agent/value_gradient.yaml:14 sets `clip_action: null`, so `do_clip` is False (line 197) and the clip is not even in the graph. When forced on at the signatures.yaml value of 10.0 in an otherwise default-ish stress run on delay_jax_unstable: 0 binds in 4500 steps (max |mu| = 0.162). Under genuine divergence (x0 = 10*ones, critic_lr = 1.0, std_init = 1.0): 5135 binds in 8935 steps = 57.5% OF ALL STEPS, with |mu| pinned at exactly 10.0 — i.e. in the regime where it matters, the control is saturated for the majority of the rollout and the agent is executing a bang-bang-like policy that is not the value-gradient law, with nothing in the log saying so. recommendation: Keep the default (null) — the code comment at lines 193-196 is right that a well-initialised critic needs no clip. If actuator limits are physical, they belong in the problem statement (and in the oracle), not in a training flag.
severity: medium (inert in the value-gradient agent as shipped; silent and heavily active — 57.5% of steps — under divergence, where the executed control is not the value-gradient law)

name: Representation window exceeds [-tau, 0] by three taps (_compute_window_size adds +3)
location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:59-61 (and :86, window_length = window_size + 1)
claimed_object: The delay differential equation's state is x_t : s -> x(t+s), s in [-tau, 0]. The value V is a functional on that path space, and the exact discretisation of [-tau, 0] at step dt has ceil(tau/dt) + 1 samples.
actual_behaviour: _compute_window_size returns int(ceil(max_delay/step_size)) + 3, so window_length = ceil(tau/dt) + 4. On the Hopfield cell (tau = 0.5, dt = 0.1) the span is 0.8 against tau = 0.5, an overshoot of exactly 3.000 taps. The origin of the constant 3 is undocumented; the CTACSignatureJAX counterpart adds 1 instead, so the two agents differentiate feature maps of paths of different length on one and the same plant. Two distinct consequences follow. (i) The samples at t < -tau are not part of the delay differential equation's state: the solution on [t, infinity) depends only on x_t restricted to [-tau, 0] and on the future control, so the true value functional is provably constant along those coordinates and they are unidentifiable from any temporal-difference data. (ii) At episode start the extra taps do not exist at all and are fabricated by _fill_buffer_initial's padding branch (:166-169) as a constant extension of phi(-tau); MEASURED with a genuinely non-constant initial path phi(s) = sin(3s), the three fabricated taps deviate from any continuation of phi by up to 0.829, and the basepoint data[0] consumed by the origin_augmentation ramp channel is the plateau value rather than a state of the plant.

With kind=raw_history, degree=1 (features are literally the flat window, so each tap is one readable coordinate), 8 episodes of LSTD on the scalar linear delay differential equation (tau=1.0, dt=0.1, seed 7) resolve a 14-tap window of which 3 lie outside [-tau, 0]. Sum |theta| on the three unidentifiable taps = 0.1632 against 0.3751 on the eleven delay-differential-equation-state taps: 30.3% of the learned critic's L1 weight sits on coordinates the value functional cannot depend on. The padding fabrication was measured separately (max deviation 0.829 on phi = sin(3s)).
logged: No. The resolved window size is never printed, never compared against tau, and never recorded in the run metadata. The +3 carries no comment. Nothing in the code or configs states that the window is 30-60% longer than [-tau, 0].

State the discretisation explicitly: the window is the exact tau/dt-tap sampling of x_t, with span (window_length-1)*dt = tau by construction. Assert that identity at construction and log the resolved (tau, dt, window_length, span) triple into the run context. Where tau/dt is not an integer, the ceiling genuinely overshoots by less than one tap; that residual is a legitimate discretisation and should be commented as such, quantified as span - tau < dt. Independently, once the window is exact, _fill_buffer_initial's padding branch can no longer fire for a history buffer of the correct length; retain the branch as an assertion rather than a silent constant extension.

name: LSTD accumulator applies the discount unconditionally, ignoring discount.discounted

claimed_object: The continuous-time temporal-difference residual is delta = r - V/tau_discount + dV/dt. The discount.discounted flag selects whether the -V/tau term is present; conf/agent/value_gradient.yaml declares discounted: false, i.e. the undiscounted residual delta = r + dV/dt.
actual_behaviour: The semi-gradient path honours the flag: critic_loss computes td_error = reward + (V_next - V_t)/dt and only subtracts V_t/tau under `if discounted:`. The LSTD path does not: line 308 unconditionally forms diff = (phi_n - phi_t)/dt - phi_c/tau, with no reference to self.discount.discounted. Setting algorithm.lstd: true therefore silently switches the estimator to a discounted fixed point that the configuration explicitly disclaims, using a tau value (100.0 in value_gradient.yaml, 1.0 in signatures.yaml) that the undiscounted setting leaves nominally inert. Two solvers behind one flag solve two different equations.
fires_in_practice: MEASURED. 183 transitions collected from 10 real episodes on the scalar linear delay differential equation (depth-2 signature, d = 12, lstd_forget = 1.0, lstd_reg = 1e-3), then both LSTD systems built offline from the identical transition set. At the shipped value_gradient.yaml tau = 100.0: ||theta_code|| = 1.696e6 against ||theta_undiscounted|| = 1.722e6, relative difference 1.47%, cosine 0.999999. At tau = 1.0 (the signatures.yaml value): ||theta_code|| = 5.697e5 against 1.722e6, relative difference 67.4%, cosine 0.9910. The defect binds whenever lstd is enabled and its magnitude is set by a parameter the user believes is disabled.
logged: No. Neither the residual actually solved nor the tau in force is printed. The block comment at :291-304 states the residual as "delta = r + theta^T[(phi_next-phi_t)/dt - phi_t/tau]", i.e. it documents the discounted form as if it were unconditional, so the code and its comment agree with each other and both disagree with the configuration.
recommendation: Gate the LSTD discount term on the same flag the semi-gradient path reads: form diff = (phi_n - phi_t)/dt and subtract phi_c/tau only when self.discount.discounted is true. Better, hoist the residual into one shared function used by both solvers, so the two estimators cannot drift apart again. Log the residual in force (discounted or undiscounted, and the tau value) once at agent construction. Note the accompanying mathematical point that should be stated in the code: with discounted: false the temporal-difference operator has constant functions in its kernel, so V is determined only up to an additive constant; the control u* = -(1/2) R^{-1} g^T grad V is invariant to that gauge, but the LSTD normal equations are singular by construction and the ridge selects the representative. That is the correct place to state it, not a comment describing a discount the flag disables.

name: lstd_reg is an absolute ridge in one branch and a relative ridge in the other; the same nominal value differs by eight orders of magnitude
location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:727/729 (rank branch, relative) against :734/736 (full-rank branch, absolute)
claimed_object: Tikhonov regularisation of the LSTD system, declared in conf/agent/value_gradient.yaml as a single scalar lstd_reg: 1.0e-3 with the comment "Tikhonov regularisation on the LSTD system (M + reg*I)", i.e. one parameter with one meaning.
actual_behaviour: When lstd_rank == 0 the solve is -solve(M + reg*I, b): an ABSOLUTE ridge, whose effect depends entirely on the scale of M. When lstd_rank > 0 the solve is -solve(Mk + reg*|trace(Mk)/rank|*I, bk): a RELATIVE, scale-aware ridge. The same lstd_reg: 1e-3 therefore means two incomparable regularisation strengths depending on an unrelated flag. Compounding this, M and b are accumulated as unnormalised sums over transitions (:309-313) with exponential forgetting (:407-409) rather than as means, so ||M|| grows with the number of transitions seen: the absolute ridge's effective strength decays over training in a way no line states, and lstd_forget silently re-scales it. The system it regularises is numerically singular: cond(M) = 4.283e21 in float64 (machine epsilon 2.220e-16), so the unregularised solve carries no significant digits and the ridge is not a numerical nicety but the operator that selects which solution is returned.
fires_in_practice: MEASURED. LSTD system after 12 real episodes on the scalar linear delay differential equation (depth-2 signature, d = 12): ||M||_2 = 3.876e8, smallest singular value 9.05e-14, cond(M) = 4.283e21, trace(M)/d = -3.004e7. The shipped absolute ridge 1e-3 has relative strength ridge/||M||_2 = 2.58e-12, while 4 of 12 singular values lie below 1e-3, so it acts only on the null subspace. Non-monotonicity in reg is MEASURED on the fixed (M, b), confirming the recorded prior: ||theta|| = 2.776e6 (reg=1e-8), 2.776e6 (1e-6), 2.788e6 (1e-4), 2.902e6 (1e-3), 4.820e6 (1e-2, a rise), 1.337e6 (1e-1), 1.103e5 (1.0). The branch discrepancy is MEASURED on the same system: at lstd_rank=3 the effective ridge is 1e-3 * 1.201e8 = 1.201e5, a factor 1.201e8 larger than the full-rank branch's 1e-3; at lstd_rank=5 it is 7.21e4, a factor 7.21e7 larger.
logged: No. Neither cond(M), nor the ridge's relative strength, nor which branch was taken, nor the number of transitions folded into M is ever reported. The LinAlgError fallbacks at :728 and :735 substitute lstsq silently. The configuration comment presents lstd_reg as one parameter with one meaning.
recommendation: Make the regularisation scale-relative and identical in both branches: lam = lstd_reg * |trace(M)|/d in the full-rank branch, matching the rank branch's convention, so lstd_reg is a dimensionless knob whose meaning does not depend on lstd_rank, on the transition count, or on lstd_forget. Accumulate M, b, C as running MEANS (divide by _lstd_n) rather than unnormalised sums, so the ridge's effect is stationary over training. Log, at every episode-end solve: cond(M), the effective lam, lam/||M||_2, the branch taken, and the number of singular values below lam — a singular value count and a condition number of 4e21 are precisely the signal that the ridge is choosing the answer. Report a warning when the LinAlgError fallback fires. Given the measured non-monotonicity, the ridge's effect on the fixed point must be stated in the write-up, not merely tuned: record the theta-versus-reg sweep alongside any LSTD result.

name: training.clip_action bounds the control away from the Doya law and confounds the actor-critic against the value gradient
location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:197-206 (opt-in, null by default) and src/agents/signatures_jax.py:358, :731, :977 (clip_action: 10.0 in conf/agent/signatures.yaml)
claimed_object: The greedy control u* = -(1/2) R^{-1} g(x_t)^T grad_{x(t)} V(x_t), the unconstrained minimiser of the Hamiltonian for the objective J = integral of r(x, u) = x^T Q x + u^T R u. No control constraint appears in the declared objective.
actual_behaviour: The value-gradient agent applies no clip (conf/agent/value_gradient.yaml sets clip_action: null) and computes the exact law. The actor-critic applies jnp.clip(u, -10, 10) componentwise. On the question of whether the clipped control remains the argmax of anything: it does, but of a different problem. R = 0.1*I in every environment shipped (src/envs/delayed_hopfield_network.py:100, src/envs/platoon.py:95, the R entries of the JAXDDEEnv configs), and for diagonal R the Hamiltonian u^T R u + (grad V)^T g u is separable across control components, so the componentwise clip is exactly the argmin over the box [-10, 10]^m. The clipped control is therefore the exact greedy control of the BOX-CONSTRAINED optimal control problem — a problem whose constraint appears nowhere in J. The consequence is not that the actor-critic is wrong in isolation; it is that the two agents solve different optimal control problems, so any actor-critic-versus-value-gradient comparison at fixed representation is confounded by a constraint present on one side only. This is the exact structural twin of the divergence_threshold mismatch that conf/agent/signatures.yaml already documents and has aligned to 100.0. Were R non-diagonal, the componentwise clip would not be the constrained argmin at all and the control would be the argmax of nothing.
fires_in_practice: MEASURED. 4000 control steps over 40 real episodes of the value-gradient agent on the Hopf-unstable scalar delay differential equation (A1 = -3.0, tau = 1.0, a*tau = 3.0 > pi/2, clip_action = None so the exact law is observed): |u| median 1.672, p90 7.464, p99 13.209, max 15.673. 288 of 4000 steps (7.20%) exceed 10.0 and would be clipped at the actor-critic's configured bound. At a bound of 1.0, 2550 of 4000 steps (63.75%) would be clipped.
logged: No. The clip is applied inside jitted code and never reports. Neither the activation count nor the most extreme pre-clip |u| is recorded. The comment at value_gradient_jax.py:193-196 asserts the law is "naturally bounded (dV/dx ~ 0 at init)", which describes initialisation only and is contradicted by the measured p99 of 13.2 on a trained-in-progress critic.
recommendation: Set clip_action: null in conf/agent/signatures.yaml so the actor-critic deploys the exact Doya law, matching the value gradient and removing the confound — the same alignment already applied to divergence_threshold. If a bound is genuinely required to keep an unstable plant numerically finite, it must be (i) identical on both agents, (ii) declared as part of the objective (J is then the box-constrained problem, and the write-up must say so, noting that the clip is the exact constrained argmin only because R is diagonal), and (iii) instrumented: warn on first activation, DEBUG thereafter, recording the count, the fraction of steps affected, and the largest pre-clip |u|. A control law that is silently saturated on 7% of steps is not the law the results claim to evaluate. Note that conf/agent/signatures.yaml is owned by a parallel workflow; this item is a recommendation to that owner, not an edit made here.

name: training.divergence_threshold truncates episodes silently, and a truncated episode's cost is not the cost of a completed one
location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:628 (and src/agents/CSAC_jax.py:634; the actor-critic's counterpart in signatures_jax.py)
claimed_object: J = integral over the episode horizon [0, max_time] of the discounted running reward r(x(t), u(t)). Every episode is an integral over the same horizon, so episodic costs are comparable across episodes and across agents.
actual_behaviour: _is_episode_done returns True as soon as ||x|| > divergence_threshold, terminating the episode. The reward is accumulated per step (train() :525), so a truncated episode integrates over a strictly shorter horizon than max_time and its cost_episodic is therefore LESS negative than the completed integral would be — the clamp makes divergence look cheap, which is the precise failure mode the project rule anticipates: the clamp regularises the very regime under study. Two further couplings matter. (i) The threshold differs in meaning between the two agents whenever normalize_entries is enabled: signatures_jax.py:93 sets training.scale = training.divergence_threshold, so the clamp is wired to a normalisation constant and moving one moves the other (conf/agent/signatures.yaml documents this). (ii) The bound is NOT applied during _evaluate_noiseless, which calls _is_episode_done(time_only=True) (:684), so the checkpoint-selection metric integrates the full horizon while the training metric does not — two differently-defined costs under one name.
fires_in_practice: MEASURED, and the firing rate is a direct function of the threshold value. 40 real episodes on the Hopf-unstable scalar delay differential equation (A1 = -3.0, tau = 1.0, dt = 0.1, max_time = 10.0, seed 42). At divergence_threshold = 100.0 (the value both agents now ship): 0 of 40 episodes truncated, 0 NaN terminations, but max ||x|| reaches 81.2, i.e. 81% of the bound — the clamp does not bind on this run yet is close enough that another seed, a longer run, or a less stable cell would trip it. At divergence_threshold = 50.0 (the actor-critic's previous value): 4 of 40 episodes truncated (10%), at ||x|| = 56.1, 56.5, 52.0, 50.4, in episodes 0, 1, 2 and 3; max ||x|| 66.7. Changing only this constant therefore changes 10% of the episodic costs on a real cell. On the saturating Hopfield cell (tanh bounds the plant) 25 real episodes give max ||x|| = 1.414 against a bound of 100: the clamp is genuinely inert there.
logged: No. Line 628 returns True with no print, no warning, and no counter. Nothing downstream distinguishes an episode that ran to max_time from one cut at 10% of it; cost_episodic and n_steps are recorded but n_steps is never checked against the expected step count. The only diagnostic in the loop is the separate NaN detector (:554-558), which does print.
recommendation: Instrument the bound to the project standard: warn on first activation, DEBUG thereafter, recording the episode index, the simulation time at the cut, the fraction of the horizon completed, and the ||x|| that tripped it. Record a per-episode `truncated` boolean and the completed-horizon fraction in metrics_history, and exclude or separately mark truncated episodes wherever cost_episodic is plotted or aggregated — a mean over episodes of unequal horizon is not an estimate of J. State in the write-up that episodic costs from truncated episodes are lower bounds on the true integral. The measured 81% of bound at threshold 100 means the current setting is on the edge for unstable cells and must be reported with any result on those cells rather than assumed inert; the Hopfield cell's measured 1.4 shows the bound is legitimately inert there and can be documented as such.

name: noise.smooth builds a Gaussian-process exploration path whose kernel is numerically the identity: the delivered exploration is white noise
location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:410-447 (and signatures_jax.py:662); conf/agent/value_gradient.yaml noise.length_scale: 0.002, conf/agent/signatures.yaml noise.length_scale: 0.02
claimed_object: A smooth exploration path: the code samples a Gaussian process with a squared-exponential kernel k(t, t') = exp(-|t-t'|^2/(2 l^2)) so that the control applied to the delay differential equation is a continuous, correlated path in time, and the resulting state window is a path of bounded variation whose signature is the object the theory addresses.
actual_behaviour: The kernel is evaluated on the control grid ts = arange(0, max_time + 5*dt, dt), so the smallest off-diagonal entry is k(t, t+dt) = exp(-dt^2/(2 l^2)). At the shipped value_gradient.yaml length_scale = 0.002 with dt = 0.1 this is exp(-1250), which underflows to EXACTLY 0.0 in float64: the covariance matrix is bit-for-bit the identity, the 1e-6 Cholesky jitter is added to the identity, and L @ white_noise returns (up to the 1e-6 jitter) the white noise unchanged. The agent constructs a 155x155 matrix and Choleskys it to reproduce its input. The declared smooth exploration is i.i.d. white noise. This is not a tuning matter: an exploration that is white in continuous time means the controlled path is not the smooth object the signature theory addresses, and the length_scale parameter is inoperative across its entire small range. A second, minor defect sits in the same block: gp_sample is scaled by self._sigma_effective (:445), which at _on_episode_start time still holds the value written by the PREVIOUS episode's last _select_action call, so under schedule 'linear_decay' or 'adaptive' the noise trajectory is scaled by a stale sigma (inert under schedule: constant, which both live configs use).
fires_in_practice: MEASURED. value_gradient.yaml settings (length_scale = 0.002, dt = 0.1, max_time = 15.0): k(t, t+dt) = 0.0 exactly, max off-diagonal |K - I| = 0.0 exactly, lag-1 autocorrelation of the drawn sample +0.0673 — indistinguishable from white noise. signatures.yaml settings (length_scale = 0.02, dt = 0.1): k(t, t+dt) = 3.727e-06, max off-diagonal |K - I| = 3.727e-06, lag-1 autocorrelation +0.0673 — also effectively white. Only at dt = 0.05 with length_scale = 0.02 does the kernel become non-trivial (k = 0.0439), and even there the lag-1 autocorrelation measures +0.0690. Both shipped configurations therefore deliver white exploration while declaring smooth: true.
logged: No. Nothing reports the realised correlation length, the ratio l/dt, or the fact that K is the identity. The Cholesky fallback at :431-437 prints only on LinAlgError, which cannot occur for the identity.
recommendation: The parameter that governs smoothness is the ratio l/dt, not l. Assert at episode start that length_scale >= a few multiples of step_size (l/dt >= 2, say, giving k(t, t+dt) = exp(-1/8) = 0.88) and raise, or at minimum warn, when l/dt is small enough that the kernel is numerically diagonal — the present configurations sit at l/dt = 0.02 and 0.2. Log the realised k(t, t+dt) and the sample's lag-1 autocorrelation once per run so the exploration's regularity is auditable. If white exploration is in fact intended, delete the Gaussian-process machinery and say so, since building and factorising a 155x155 identity to draw white noise misrepresents the object in both the code and any write-up that cites smooth exploration. Separately, scale gp_sample by the sigma computed for the episode about to start rather than the stale _sigma_effective left by the previous episode.

name: training.scale rescales the window but the control law omits the chain-rule factor, inflating u by exactly `scale`
location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:163/166/171 and :336/346/351/450/691 (the window is divided by scale) against :199-206 (_select_action_jit differentiates with respect to the SCALED endpoint and applies the result as if it were grad_{x(t)} V)
claimed_object: u* = -(1/2) R^{-1} g(x_t)^T grad_{x(t)} V(x_t), where grad_{x(t)} V is Dupire's vertical derivative — the derivative with respect to the window's endpoint in the plant's TRUE units.
actual_behaviour: Every sample entering the representation buffer is divided by training.scale, so the critic is a function of the scaled window p/s while the temporal-difference residual is driven by the reward in TRUE units (env_rk_jax.py:88 computes r from the unscaled state). The learned critic therefore satisfies V_hat_s(p/s) = V(p), where V is the true value functional, whence grad_{x(t)} V = (1/s) * (d V_hat_s / d p_scaled). _select_action_jit takes grad_V_fn(critic_params, path_data) with path_data the SCALED buffer (:239 via _get_path_data), reads end_gradient = grad_path[-1], and forms u = 1/2 * inv(R) @ B.T @ end_gradient with no 1/s factor. The deployed control is therefore s * u*, an exact factor-`scale` inflation of the Doya law. The inconsistency is visible within the single expression at :199-203: B is evaluated at x_current = self.wrapper.state.x, the UNSCALED state (correct for the plant, and load-bearing for the state-dependent get_B of the platoon environment), while the gradient contracted against it is taken with respect to the scaled endpoint. Two different unit systems meet in one matrix product.
fires_in_practice: NOT MEASURED TO FIRE, and it cannot currently fire: training.scale = 1.0 in every shipped configuration (grep over conf/ returns scale: 1.0 in value_gradient.yaml, signatures.yaml, base_jax.yaml, CSAC_jax.yaml, CTAC_jax.yaml, CTAC_sig_jax.yaml, CTAC_sig_MG_1D.yaml, CTAC_sig_chemical.yaml, CTAC_jax_mackey_glass.yaml, CTAC_simple.yaml, CTAC_critic_oracle.yaml, CTAC_actor_oracle.yaml, sanity_check_actor.yaml), so s = 1 and the missing factor is unity. The defect is latent, not active. The route by which it becomes active is short and already present in the codebase: signatures_jax.py:93 and CSAC_jax.py:209 both set self.scale = self.divergence_threshold when network.normalize_entries is true, which would set s = 100.0 and inflate the control law hundredfold. The claim above is analytical (the chain rule), not measured; a probe holding the critic parameters fixed across s = 1, 2, 10 returned u = 1.000, 0.750, 0.550, but that probe conflates the missing factor with the change in the learned V and is NOT offered as evidence — it is reported here only to record that no measurement of the live defect was performed, because at s = 1 there is nothing to measure.
logged: No. The scaled problem's mathematical status is stated nowhere: no comment says whether the learned V is the value of the true plant expressed in scaled coordinates or the value of a rescaled plant, and no line reports the units of the reported cost. The absence matters because the two readings imply different corrections.
recommendation: Divide the endpoint gradient by training.scale before contracting it against B: end_gradient = grad_path[-1] / scale, with a comment deriving the factor from V_hat_s(p/s) = V(p). Add a regression test asserting that the deployed u is invariant to training.scale for a fixed plant state — a two-line test that pins the covariance permanently. Until that lands, either assert training.scale == 1.0 at construction or state at the top of the agent that scale != 1.0 is unsupported, so that enabling network.normalize_entries cannot silently multiply the control law by 100 through the signatures_jax.py:93 / CSAC_jax.py:209 coupling. name: The initial path is narrowed to float32 in an otherwise float64 pipeline, leaving the window mixed-precision
location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:163, :166, :171 (dtype=np.float32 in _fill_buffer_initial) against src/representations/factory.py:65/73/89 (RepresentationBuffer and DequeBuffer declared float64) — code-review finding F-E1, commits 07b8d4a, 7b1153e
claimed_object: The initial condition phi, an element of C([-tau, 0], R^d), sampled onto the window at the pipeline's working precision. JAX x64 is enabled and every other write to the buffer is float64 (RepresentationBuffer.append casts to self.dtype = np.float64), so the window should be uniformly float64.
actual_behaviour: _fill_buffer_initial writes the initial path with an explicit dtype=np.float32 on all three of its append paths. DequeBuffer.to_array then reconstitutes the window at the declared float64, which upcasts the already-rounded values and conceals the narrowing: the array's dtype reads float64 while its low-order bits are gone. Because subsequent appends during the rollout are float64, the window is MIXED precision — the taps belonging to phi carry float32 rounding and the taps accumulated after t = 0 carry float64 — so the representation's accuracy is discontinuous across the episode-start boundary and drifts as the window slides. This is not the deliberate float32-for-comparison option: SlidingSignatureJAX exposes dtype as a selectable parameter (dynamic_signature.py:124, defaulting to float64 with the comment "float32 selectable for comparison"), and this narrowing bypasses it with a hard-coded literal. CTACSignatureJAX explicitly declines to mirror it, and says why at signatures_jax.py:266-269: "the float32 rounding is irreversible".
fires_in_practice: MEASURED, on every episode of every value-gradient run — the narrowing is unconditional. Magnitude, on the scalar linear delay differential equation with a non-constant initial path phi(s) = sin(3s), tau = 1.0, dt = 0.1, depth-2 signature with time and origin augmentation: max |window_float32 - window_float64| = 1.906e-08; induced relative error in the signature = 1.074e-08, against float64 machine epsilon 2.220e-16, i.e. 4.84e7 times the round-off the rest of the pipeline carries. Buffer state confirmed directly: after _fill_buffer_initial the stored item dtypes are {float32} while the declared DequeBuffer dtype is float64 and to_array() reports float64; after one subsequent append the stored dtypes are {float32, float64}, which is the mixed-precision window. The absolute magnitude (1e-8 relative) is far below the temporal-difference and exploration noise, so no reported number is currently expected to move; the defect is a silent, unnecessary precision loss and a latent hazard for any gradient-sensitive diagnostic, not a demonstrated corruption of the science.
logged: No. The dtype literal carries no comment, nothing reports the window's realised precision, and the float64 dtype reported by to_array() actively masks the narrowing from any reader who inspects the array.
recommendation: Remove the three dtype=np.float32 literals so _fill_buffer_initial writes at the buffer's declared dtype, exactly as RepresentationBuffer.append already does — the sole caller of this method already owns a float64 buffer, so this is a deletion, not a change of policy. Route any genuine float32 comparison through the dtype parameter SlidingSignatureJAX already exposes, which keeps the window uniform. Add an assertion in RepresentationBuffer.append that the incoming dtype matches self.dtype, so a narrowing cannot be re-introduced and then hidden by to_array's upcast. Note that this measurement re-confirms an existing code-review finding (F-E1) that remains live in the working tree.

name: dV/dt is a first-order forward difference paired with a right-endpoint reward and a left-endpoint discount; the order is never stated and consistency is never checked
location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:259-265 (critic_loss) with src/envs/env_rk_jax.py:88 (reward evaluated at the end of the step)
claimed_object: The continuous-time temporal-difference residual delta = r(x(t), u(t)) - V(x_t)/tau_discount + dV/dt, with all three terms evaluated at the same instant t.
actual_behaviour: dV/dt is computed as (V_next - V_t)/dt, a first-order forward difference equal to dV/dt + (dt/2) V'' + O(dt^2) at t. The reward, however, is not evaluated at t: env_rk_jax.py:88 computes reward = -(final_state.x^T Q final_state.x + u^T R u) from final_state, i.e. from x(t+dt) after the RK4 sub-step scan, so r is the right-endpoint value r(x(t+dt), u(t)). The discount term uses V_t, the left endpoint. The residual therefore evaluates its three terms at three different points of the interval: r at t+dt, the difference quotient consistently at t+dt only if read as a backward difference, and -V/tau at t. Every mismatch is O(dt), the same order as the scheme itself, so the residual remains a consistent first-order discretisation and no term is wrong — but the scheme is first-order where the plant is integrated at fourth order (RK4, resolution sub-steps), and at the shipped dt = 0.1 the O(dt) error is not negligible relative to the quantities being fit. This is a necessary discretisation of a continuous object, correctly classified as legitimate; what is missing is that the arithmetic be stated and the convergence checked. Nothing in the code names the order, states which endpoint each term is evaluated at, or tests that the residual converges as dt -> 0. A related, separate concern: _evaluate_noiseless accumulates total_cost += float(reward) * self.env.step_size (:693), a left-rectangle rule over a right-endpoint reward — also first-order, also unstated — and truncates the infinite-horizon J at max_time = 15.0 with no statement of the truncation error.
fires_in_practice: MEASURED as present on every step of every run — this is the training residual itself, not a guard. The endpoint mismatch is established by reading env_rk_jax.py:88 (reward built from final_state.x, the post-scan state) against value_gradient_jax.py:262 (V_t and V_next straddling the same step). The magnitude of the O(dt) error at dt = 0.1 was NOT measured: no dt-refinement study exists in the repository, and none was run here.
logged: Partially, and misleadingly. The residual's algebraic form is commented (configs.py:53 documents "δ = r + V̇ − V/τ"), but no comment states that V̇ is a first-order forward difference, that r is a right-endpoint value, or that the three terms sit at different points of the interval. No convergence or consistency statement accompanies any reported result.
recommendation: State the scheme where it is implemented: a comment at critic_loss naming the order (first-order in dt), the endpoint of each term, and the resulting O(dt) consistency error, so a reader can weigh it against the fourth-order plant integration. Run and record a dt-refinement study — halve step_size and confirm the residual and the learned control converge at the expected first-order rate — since the order is currently asserted by inspection and measured by nothing; this is the check that converts a legitimate discretisation into a defensible one. Consider evaluating the reward at the left endpoint x(t) (or a midpoint), which would align r with V_t and -V_t/tau and make the residual a clean forward-Euler discretisation at t, at no cost. Apply the same treatment to _evaluate_noiseless: name the quadrature (left rectangle, first order) and state the horizon-truncation error incurred by stopping J at max_time.

name: _sample_initial_state draws a point from a normal distribution; the delay differential equation's initial condition is a path
location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:137-140, consumed at :490-491 under `if not self.algorithm.fix_initial_state`; the point becomes a constant path at src/envs/env_rk_jax.py:76-77
claimed_object: The initial condition of a delay differential equation is a PATH phi in C([-tau, 0], R^d), an infinite-dimensional object. Randomising the initial condition means sampling a measure on that path space.
actual_behaviour: _sample_initial_state returns jax.random.normal(subkey, shape=(self.env.N,)) — a point in R^d, N = env.A.shape[0]. That point is passed to wrapper.reset(subkey, x0=x_init, t0=0.0) with no history_function, and JAXDDEEnv.reset's else-branch at :76-77 builds data_history = jnp.tile(self.x0, (self.buffer_size, 1)): the history buffer is filled with the SAME point at every tap. The initial path is therefore the constant path phi(s) = x_init for all s in [-tau, 0]. The sampling measure is supported on the d-dimensional submanifold of constant paths inside the infinite-dimensional C([-tau, 0], R^d) — a null set in any reasonable measure on path space. This is the same class of error as the already-diagnosed preheat (a device standing in for phi), reached from the opposite direction: the preheat overwrote phi with an uncontrolled evolution, whereas this collapses phi to a constant. The consequence for the science is specific: a value functional trained only on constant initial paths is fit on a d-dimensional slice of its domain, so nothing in the training distribution excites the history directions, which are precisely the directions H1 and H2 are about. The machinery to do this correctly already exists and is used elsewhere — reset accepts a history_function (env_rk_jax.py:61, :71-73, vmapped over the buffer's past times), and src/envs/mackey_glass_1D.py:149/157, run/study/feature_conditioning_check.py:39 and run/study/least_squares_value_fit_check.py:51/74 all pass one. The agent never does.
fires_in_practice: NOT MEASURED TO FIRE on any shipped configuration: algorithm.fix_initial_state is true in both conf/agent/value_gradient.yaml and conf/agent/signatures.yaml, so the `if not self.algorithm.fix_initial_state` branch at :490 is never taken and _sample_initial_state is dead in the live runs. The branch's behaviour was nonetheless established by execution rather than inference: resetting with x0 and no history_function and then calling _fill_buffer_initial yields a window whose taps are all equal to x0 (distinct rows = 1 before any append), confirming the constant-path collapse. The defect is latent and fires the moment fix_initial_state is set false — which is exactly what an initial-condition-randomisation study would do.
logged: No. Nothing states that the sampled initial condition is a constant path, and the branch produces no output distinguishing it from a genuine path sample. The comment at :504-509 correctly describes the fixed-phi case ("The DDE initial condition is the initial PATH phi on [-tau, 0] ... set at reset via history_function, or constant x_init") and names the constant-x_init fallback, but does not note that the sampling branch has no route to anything else.
recommendation: Replace _sample_initial_state with a sampler on path space and pass it through the history_function argument reset already accepts: draw phi from an explicit, documented measure on C([-tau, 0], R^d) — a Gaussian process with a stated kernel and correlation length is the natural choice and would reuse the machinery already in _on_episode_start — and call wrapper.reset(subkey, x0=phi(0.0), t0=0.0, history_function=phi), so x0 and the history are the same object by construction rather than by coincidence. State the measure in the run context alongside the seed, since the initial-condition distribution is part of the problem specification and not an implementation detail. If constant paths are genuinely wanted for a particular study, that is a legitimate choice of measure and should be named as such (a constant-path measure), not arrived at silently through an unset default. Until a path sampler exists, assert that fix_initial_state is true rather than leaving a branch that quietly collapses the initial condition to a point.

name: The dt <= 1e-9 guard substitutes a fabricated step size rather than failing
location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:348-349, mirrored at src/agents/base_jax.py:243 and src/agents/signatures_jax.py:489
claimed_object: dt is the temporal-difference step size, an exact quantity read from env.step_size and appearing as the denominator of the difference quotient (V_next - V_t)/dt in the residual delta = r - V/tau + dV/dt.
actual_behaviour: `dt = self.env.step_size; if dt <= 1e-9: dt = 1e-4  # Avoid division by zero` replaces the true step size with the unrelated literal 1e-4. This is not a floor: a floor would clamp dt to the smallest representable sensible value and be off by that amount, whereas this substitutes a number five orders of magnitude away from the guard threshold and bearing no relation to the plant's actual integration step. Were it to fire, the difference quotient would be divided by a fabricated denominator and the residual scaled by 1e5 relative to its correct value, silently — and the same fabricated dt is passed into the loss weighting (0.5 * td_error^2 * dt) and the reported metrics (StepMetrics loss and reward are both multiplied by dt at :390). The construct is dead in practice, but it is dead by accident of configuration rather than by any argument: nothing prevents a future environment from carrying a small step_size, and the guard's threshold and its replacement value are not related to each other.
fires_in_practice: NOT MEASURED TO FIRE, and it cannot fire on any shipped configuration: dt = env.step_size is a construction-time constant taken from the environment configs, whose values are 0.1 (hopfield_nonlinear, linear_dde_scalar) and 0.05 (platoon_h1h2), each seven to eight orders of magnitude above the 1e-9 threshold. The branch was never taken in any of the runs performed for this audit (40-episode runs on the Hopf-unstable scalar delay differential equation and 25-episode runs on the Hopfield cell). It is genuinely inert today.
logged: No — and this is the substantive point rather than the firing rate. The comment reads only "# Avoid division by zero", which states the intent but not the consequence, and the project rule permits an unlogged clamp only when it is provably inert AND carries a comment saying why. This one is inert for a contingent reason (no shipped environment has a small step size), not a provable one, and its comment does not say so.
recommendation: Delete the substitution and replace it with a construction-time validation: raise in __init__ if env.step_size is not strictly positive and finite. A step size of zero is a configuration error that should stop the run loudly at construction, not be papered over with 1e-4 in the middle of a jitted training step where it would silently rescale the residual by 1e5. This costs nothing — dt is a constant, so the check belongs where the constant is read, not on the hot path — and removes a construct that is currently harmless only by luck. Apply the same treatment to the two mirrors in base_jax.py:243 and signatures_jax.py:489 so the pattern does not survive by copy.

name: signature.state_augmentation and signature.time_origin are dead parameters in the representation path
location: src/configs.py:83, :85 (SignatureConfig fields) against src/representations/factory.py:28-53 (make_representation's parameter list) and src/representations/signature.py:22-42 (SignatureRepresentation.__init__)
claimed_object: Configuration fields are the run's specification: a parameter present in SignatureConfig and settable from YAML is expected to reach the object it names. state_augmentation nominally appends x(t) to the signature; time_origin nominally sets the normalised window length T used by the time channel t in [0, T] and the origin ramp (X_0/T) * t.
actual_behaviour: Neither field is forwarded by the value-gradient agent. _init_networks (value_gradient_jax.py:87-96) passes kind, window_length, n_state, depth, degree, time_augmentation, origin_augmentation and bias to make_representation, whose signature accepts exactly {kind, window_length, n_state, depth, degree, time_augmentation, origin_augmentation, bias, dtype} — state_augmentation and time_origin are not among them. SignatureRepresentation.__init__ likewise accepts only {depth, window_length, n_state, time_augmentation, origin_augmentation, bias, dtype} and constructs SlidingSignatureJAX without time_origin, which therefore takes its default of 1.0 unconditionally. Setting either field in a YAML file changes nothing and reports nothing. On the substance of state_augmentation, the brief's suspicion is well founded and is a conditioning matter rather than tidiness: when origin_augmentation is enabled the ramp channel's total increment is exactly X_0 (dynamic_signature.py:200-203, data[0] * elapsed_fraction), and the signature's depth-1 terms already contain the increment X_T - X_0 of the state channel, so the endpoint x(t) is recoverable from the depth-1 signature and appending it adds a linearly dependent direction to the feature map — which matters given the measured cond(M) = 4.283e21 of the LSTD system. That the field is dead means this redundancy is currently untestable rather than absent.
fires_in_practice: NOT MEASURED TO FIRE, and provably cannot in this path: verified by introspection at runtime that make_representation's parameter list is ['kind', 'window_length', 'n_state', 'depth', 'degree', 'time_augmentation', 'origin_augmentation', 'bias', 'dtype'] and SignatureRepresentation.__init__'s is ['depth', 'window_length', 'n_state', 'time_augmentation', 'origin_augmentation', 'bias', 'dtype']; that the string 'state_augmentation' does not occur anywhere in value_gradient_jax.py; that the string 'time_origin' does not occur anywhere in value_gradient_jax.py; and that no file under conf/ sets time_origin (grep -rl returns nothing). conf/agent/signatures.yaml does set state_augmentation: false, which is the value the dead field would have taken anyway.
logged: No. Hydra accepts both fields silently, so a study that sets signature.time_origin: 2.0 or signature.state_augmentation: true would run to completion, record the setting in its metadata, and produce results identical to the unset run — the failure mode is a recorded parameter that the artefact provenance would attribute a difference to.
recommendation: Resolve each field in the direction its intended semantics warrant rather than leaving both silently ignored. For time_origin: it rescales only the time channel, whose scaling is absorbed by the downstream linear readout (as dynamic_signature.py:196 already argues), so it is genuinely inert and should be deleted from SignatureConfig with a one-line comment recording why — an inert parameter may remain unlogged only if a comment states the argument for its inertness, which is exactly what is missing. For state_augmentation: it is not inert, it is unimplemented; either thread it through make_representation and SignatureRepresentation so the redundancy claim above can be tested and measured, or delete the field. Whichever is chosen, add a validation step that rejects unknown or unconsumed keys in the signature config block, so a parameter that reaches no object fails the run at startup instead of being recorded in metadata as though it had taken effect.

name: The adaptive noise schedule's clip and epsilon are inert at the shipped configuration but uncommented
location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:223 (and the identical construct at signatures_jax.py:387)
claimed_object: Exploration magnitude sigma_effective, a data-collection knob. It does not enter the value functional, the residual, or the control law, so it cannot alter a reported value directly — it changes only which states are visited.
actual_behaviour: Under noise.schedule == 'adaptive', noise_scale = jnp.clip((V_TARGET - V_t) / (V_TARGET - V_BAD + 1e-6), 0.1, 1.0). Two constructs sit in one line and warrant different verdicts. The 1e-6 is a denominator epsilon guarding V_TARGET - V_BAD, which at the shipped V_target = 0.0 and V_bad = -10.0 evaluates to 10.0: the epsilon shifts the denominator by one part in 1e7, a relative perturbation far below any quantity the exploration schedule resolves. It is genuinely inert and would qualify as an acceptable safety epsilon — but it carries no comment saying why, which the project rule requires of every unlogged inert clamp. The jnp.clip(..., 0.1, 1.0) is a real saturation on a live quantity: it floors the exploration at 10% of sigma and ceilings it at 100%, so a critic reporting V_t below V_BAD or above V_TARGET has its schedule truncated silently. That clamp is not inert in general; it is unreached only because no shipped configuration selects the schedule that contains it.
fires_in_practice: NOT MEASURED TO FIRE, and unreachable on every shipped configuration: noise.schedule is 'constant' in both conf/agent/value_gradient.yaml and conf/agent/signatures.yaml, so _select_action takes the else-branch at :229-231 and the adaptive block is never entered. Confirmed by grep over conf/ (schedule: constant in both agent configs) and by the 40-episode and 25-episode runs performed for this audit, all of which ran under schedule: constant. Were the schedule selected, the clip's firing rate would depend on the realised V_t distribution and has not been measured.
logged: No. Neither the epsilon nor the clip carries a comment, and neither reports when it binds. The inertness of both rests entirely on a configuration value set in a different file, which no comment at the call site records.
recommendation: Comment the epsilon with the argument for its inertness — V_TARGET - V_BAD = 10.0 at the shipped constants, so 1e-6 perturbs the denominator by 1e-7 relative, below any scale the schedule resolves — which is precisely the statement the project rule requires before an inert clamp may go unlogged. Treat the clip differently, because it is a saturation on a live quantity rather than a safety epsilon: if the adaptive schedule is ever enabled, instrument it to the same standard as the other clamps in this audit (warn on first activation, DEBUG thereafter, recording the count and the most extreme pre-clip noise_scale), since a floored exploration silently narrows the visited state distribution and therefore the data the critic is fit on. If the adaptive and linear_decay schedules are not intended for use, delete them rather than carrying two unreachable branches whose clamps are inert only by the accident of a default set elsewhere.

name: ContinuousValueGradient window over-spans tau by exactly three control steps (the unjustified "+3")
location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:59-61
claimed_object: The delay differential equation's state is the path x_t : s -> x(t+s) on EXACTLY [-tau, 0]. Its discretisation at spacing dt requires ceil(tau/dt)+1 taps, inclusive of both endpoints.
actual_behaviour: _compute_window_size returns int(np.ceil(max_delay/step_size)) + 3, and _init_networks then sets window_length = window_size + 1, so the buffer holds ceil(tau/dt)+4 taps and spans (ceil(tau/dt)+3)*dt. Measured spans versus tau: linear_dde_scalar 1.600 vs 1.000 (1.60x); platoon_h1h2 0.350 vs 0.200 (1.75x); hopfield_{linear,nonlinear,duffing} 0.800 vs 0.500 (1.60x); MG_1D_limit_cycle 6.750 vs 6.000 (1.12x); MG_1D_chaotic 17.750 vs 17.000 (1.04x). The window reaches back to -1.75 tau on the platoon. The env's own history buffer spans exactly tau in every one of these cells (measured env_span == tau), so the critic is handed a strictly larger object than the one the integrator evolves. `git log -S "+ 3 if max_delay"` returns only a02cc92 (initial import): the constant 3 has no justification in code, comment, or history.
fires_in_practice: MEASURED on all five named cells plus the three hopfield configs, by instantiating each env from conf/ under jax_enable_x64=True (matching main_unified.py:63) and evaluating the quoted formula. The over-span is unconditional — it is the resolved window on every delayed run, not an edge case.
logged: No. The resolved window_size is written silently into signature_conf; nothing prints the span, nothing compares it to tau. The `else` branch at value_gradient_jax.py:56 prints only when force_signature_window is true (the non-default).
recommendation: Replace the formula with the exact discretisation window_length = round(tau/dt) + 1 (round, not ceil — see the float32 finding), and assert (window_length-1)*dt == tau to within solver tolerance so a config whose tau is not an integer multiple of dt fails loudly rather than silently acquiring taps. If pre-history beyond -tau is ever wanted deliberately, it must be a named, documented config knob with its mathematical status stated — not a bare +3.

name: The excess taps are fabricated by constant-extending phi backwards beyond -tau, silently, on every reset
location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:146-173 (_fill_buffer_initial, pad branch at 167-171)
claimed_object: The window should contain phi in C([-tau,0], R^d) sampled at spacing dt — and nothing else. Data before -tau is not part of the delay differential equation's state and does not exist as initial data.
actual_behaviour: The env history buffer, subsampled by resolution, yields EXACTLY the correct number of taps for [-tau,0] (measured: linear_dde 6, hopfield 6, MG_1D_limit_cycle 25, platoon 5 — each equal to the exact requirement). But target_len = window_size+1 is larger, because of the +3 / +1 above, so `len(subsampled) >= target_len` is FALSE and the pad branch always fires: it prepends copies of subsampled[0] (the oldest sample, i.e. phi(-tau)) to reach target_len. The window therefore contains a constant extension of phi onto [-tau-k*dt, -tau) — invented data, not the initial path. Measured pad counts per reset: value-gradient — linear_dde_scalar 3 of 9 taps, platoon_h1h2 4 of 9, hopfield_linear 3 of 9, MG_1D_limit_cycle 3 of 28; signature agent — 1, 2, 1, 1 respectively. On the platoon the value-gradient window is 44% fabricated. This is the same class of defect as the already-diagnosed preheat: an engineering device standing in for the mathematical object. It also biases the representation specifically: a constant leading segment contributes zero increment, so the ramp/origin channel and every iterated integral see a flat prefix that phi never had.
fires_in_practice: MEASURED by executing the real reset path (JAXEnvWrapper.reset + initial_conditions + the quoted subsample/target_len logic) on linear_dde_scalar, platoon_h1h2, hopfield_linear and MG_1D_limit_cycle. The pad branch fired on 4 of 4 cells for BOTH agents; the truncate branch fired on 0 of 4. It is the universal path at every episode reset, not a fallback.
logged: No. Neither branch prints, counts, or warns. Nothing distinguishes 'window is phi' from 'window is 44% invented'.
recommendation: Once the window is fixed to round(tau/dt)+1 the pad branch becomes unreachable on a well-posed config, which is the correct end state — the subsampled history already has exactly the right length. Until then, and permanently as a guard, the branch must warn-once at WARNING with the pad count and target_len per the project's clamp rule. Better: convert it to a hard error, because reaching it means the window does not match tau and no run should proceed silently in that state.

name: Markovian fallback window of 10 taps: a magic constant imposing 1.0 s of history on a memoryless plant
location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:61 and src/agents/signatures_jax.py:163 (the `else 10` branch)
claimed_object: For double_integrator (A1 = 0, delay = 0) the plant is Markovian: the state is the point x(t) in R^2 and the value depends on x(t) alone. The exact window is 1 tap.
actual_behaviour: Both agents fall back to window_size = 10, hence window_length = 11 taps spanning 1.0 s of pre-history (measured). The critic's input is an 11-tap path where the state is a single point — 10 taps of dynamically irrelevant history. The constant 10 has no derivation; it is unrelated to any timescale of the plant (no delay exists to set one). This is not merely untidy: the feature dimension and the conditioning of the representation both scale with window length, and double_integrator is the designated H1-NEGATIVE control cell, so the null result it certifies is measured on a representation inflated by an arbitrary constant. Note conf/agent/value_gradient.yaml:49 sets window_size: 40, which this fallback silently overrides to 10 whenever force_signature_window is false (the default) — the configured value never takes effect on any cell.
fires_in_practice: MEASURED: double_integrator resolves to 11 taps for both agents (window_audit, x64 enabled). Whether the inflated window materially shifts the H1 verdict on this cell was NOT measured — that requires a 1-tap-versus-11-tap run, which this read-only audit did not perform.
logged: No. The override of the configured window_size: 40 down to 10 is entirely silent for the default force_signature_window: false.
recommendation: For a Markovian plant set window_length = 1 (the state IS the point) and let the representation degenerate accordingly, or make the fallback an explicit, documented config value rather than a literal buried in an expression. Either way, log the resolved window and state that it overrode the configured value. Re-run the double_integrator H1 cell at the corrected window before citing its negative result.

name: float32 narrowing of the initial path on the phi-loading path, in a float64 pipeline

name: origin_augmentation: the ramp channel breaks Chen's identity for the sliding window
