With a globally-consistent clock (so the time channel concatenates exactly and cannot confound the test), the un-augmented channel set (t, X) satisfies Chen at machine precision: relative residual 9.9e-17, 1.8e-16, 2.6e-16, 3.1e-16, 1.8e-16, 2.3e-16, 1.1e-15 for N = 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024. The mechanism is exact, not numerical: the ramp's slope is set by data[0], that window's own earliest sample, so a sub-window re-bases the ramp on its own start; the concatenation of the two sub-paths' augmented forms is a DIFFERENT path from the whole window's augmented form, and Chen -- which is an identity about concatenated paths -- has no purchase. Neither agent forms a signature product. dV/dt is a plain finite difference on independently recomputed signatures -- value_gradient_jax.py:262 `td_error = reward + (V_next - V_t) / dt` and signatures_jax.py:572, :542 identically. Each window is re-augmented from scratch, so the feature map remains a well-defined (if window-dependent) functional of the window. The broken identity is therefore a defect in the PAPER's lemma, not in the code path.

State the code's actual contract instead -- the feature map is recomputed per window and dV/dt is a finite difference -- so no Chen-based lemma is needed to justify the implementation. Do NOT remove the ramp on account of this: it is separately measured (below) to be what makes the endpoint linearly recoverable. Amend the dynamic_signature.py docstring to say the augmentation is applied per window and that the concatenation property does not hold across windows.

name: Signature feature Gram is numerically singular: effective rank ~5 of 30
location: src/representations/signature.py:48-51; consumed by src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:108 (linear critic readout)
claimed_object: Arribas Theorem 4.2: linear functionals of the signature are dense in the continuous functionals of the path. The critic (hidden_dims: [], i.e. a bare linear readout) realises that density by least squares on the feature Gram.
actual_behaviour: MEASURED on 400 sampled windows (n_state=2, window_length=41, depth=2, origin_augmentation=true): cond(G) = 9.400e+20 and effective rank (entropy of the normalised spectrum) = 4.95 out of a feature dimension of 30. The Gram is numerically singular in float64 -- roughly 25 of 30 directions lie at or below the double-precision noise floor. Density in the limit is not realisability at finite depth on finite data: the linear readout is identified only in ~5 directions, and whatever occupies the remaining ~25 is set by the solver's tie-breaking, not by the data. This is the effective-rank/Veronese phenomenon the 2026-06-17 note formalises, now measured on this repository's own feature map. Turning state_augmentation on barely moves it (cond 1.581e+20, effective rank 4.88 of 32) -- confirming the ill-conditioning is intrinsic to the signature features and NOT attributable to that flag.

logged: No. Nothing in the run context reports the feature dimension, the Gram conditioning, or the effective rank, so a reader cannot tell that the readout is identified in only ~1/6 of its nominal directions.
recommendation: Record cond(G) and the effective rank of the feature second moment in the run log at startup and periodically -- they are diagnostic of whether the representation is doing anything, and are currently invisible. This measurement also reframes the LSTD regularisers below: at cond ~1e20 the ridge is not a tidiness parameter, it SELECTS the solution in ~25 of 30 directions. State the truncation depth's status honestly in the write-up: depth=2 is a discretisation whose truncation error is neither bounded nor measured anywhere in the code, and the density theorem it invokes is asymptotic in depth and therefore does not license a finite-depth claim.

name: LSTD Tikhonov ridge is absolute, not scale-invariant, and inconsistent between the two branches
location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:734 (full-D branch), :725-730 (truncated-SVD branch); conf/agent/value_gradient.yaml:79-82
claimed_object: The continuous-time TD fixed point E[phi delta] = 0, solved as M theta = -b. The Tikhonov term should be a small, principled perturbation of that estimator.
actual_behaviour: The two branches regularise on INCOMPATIBLE scales. The full-D branch solves `-np.linalg.solve(self._lstd_M + self._lstd_reg * np.eye(d), self._lstd_b)` -- an ABSOLUTE ridge of 1e-3, whose meaning depends entirely on the arbitrary magnitude of M (itself set by the feature scale, the reward scale, dt and tau). The truncated branch instead uses `Mk + self._lstd_reg * abs(scale) * np.eye(rank)` with `scale = np.trace(Mk)/rank` -- a RELATIVE ridge. The same configured lstd_reg = 1e-3 therefore denotes two different perturbations depending on lstd_rank, and neither is dimensionless. Read against the measured cond(G) = 9.4e20 above, this is not a small perturbation: in the ~25 of 30 directions below the noise floor the ridge is the ONLY thing determining theta, so lstd_reg silently selects the estimator rather than stabilising it. This is consistent with the recorded non-monotonicity of the absolute ridge on this problem. lstd_rank > 0 additionally truncates the estimator to a top-k subspace -- a different estimator, not a numerical safeguard.
fires_in_practice: MEASURED to be unreachable in the current campaign: grep over conf/ shows NO configuration enables lstd (conf/agent/value_gradient.yaml:76 sets `lstd: false`, and no other agent config declares the key). The LSTD branch does not execute, so lstd_reg and lstd_rank cannot presently alter any reported number. The finding is latent, not active. The ridge's effect on theta was NOT MEASURED, the code path being off.
logged: No. Neither branch reports the ridge's magnitude relative to the spectrum of M, nor how many directions it dominates -- which, at cond ~1e20, is the whole question.
recommendation: Before ever enabling lstd, make the ridge relative and identical in both branches (e.g. reg * trace(M)/d in the full-D branch, matching the truncated branch), so lstd_reg is dimensionless and comparable across problems and across rank settings. Log the ridge's magnitude against the spectrum of M and the count of directions in which it dominates. Treat lstd_rank as an explicit estimator choice and report it as such in any result -- a truncated-SVD LSTD solution is not the LSTD solution and must not be reported under that name.

name: training.scale: the control law omits the chain-rule factor, latent behind scale = 1.0
location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:199-206 (select_action), :336 (x_scaled), :351 (append of scaled state), :450
claimed_object: u* = -(1/2) R^{-1} g(x_t)^T grad_{x(t)} V(x_t), the gradient taken with respect to the PHYSICAL endpoint x(t). (The code's +1/2 sign is CORRECT, not a defect: env_rk_jax.py:88 defines reward = -(x'Qx + u'Ru), so V is maximised and the sign flips consistently.)

name: Target-network lag contaminates dV/dt in the continuous-time TD residual
location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:259-265 (critic_loss), conf/agent/value_gradient.yaml:18 (tau_polyak: 0.01)
claimed_object: The continuous-time temporal-difference residual delta = r - V/tau_discount + dV/dt, in which dV/dt is the time derivative of ONE value functional V along the trajectory. Doya's semi-gradient prescribes a stop-gradient on V(s') — the same function, with the gradient blocked — not a second, lagged function.
actual_behaviour: Line 260-262 evaluate V_t with `critic_params` and V_next with a Polyak-averaged `target_params`, then form `td_error = reward + (V_next - V_t)/dt`. The second term is not part of the mathematics and is amplified by 1/dt = 10 at dt = 0.1. The Polyak rate tau_polyak = 0.01 keeps the target persistently lagged, so the term does not vanish during training. name: LSTD ridge is the sole selector of the solution on a numerically singular system, is absolute rather than scaled, and is unlogged

name: runge_kutta4 is second-order on the delay differential equation, not fourth
location: src/envs/env_rk_jax.py:53-59 (`runge_kutta4`), :45-51 (`dynamics`); src/utils/solver_buffer_jax.py:36-62 (`get_delayed_interpolated`, linear interpolation)

These are obtained from `get_delayed_interpolated`, which does LINEAR interpolation between the two bracketing buffer samples (line 62, `(1 - delay_frac)*x_newer + delay_frac*x_older`). Linear interpolation of the delayed argument has local error O(h^2), which caps the global order of the whole scheme at 2 regardless of the fourth-order Butcher tableau. This is the standard result for Runge-Kutta methods on delay differential equations: the order is min(p, q+1) with q the interpolant degree. The stage offsets themselves are correct (`adjusted_delay_steps = base_delay_steps - dt_offset_fraction` at line 49 gives exactly tau/h - c_i, i.e. the delayed argument measured from the step's left endpoint), so the arithmetic is right — only the order claim is wrong. The control u is additionally held constant across all RK stages and across all `resolution` sub-steps, which is a legitimate zero-order-hold sampled-data control and consistent with the discrete decision cadence.
fires_in_practice: MEASURED by a convergence study on the scalar linear delay differential equation xdot = -x - 2 x(t - 1), constant history x == 1, u == 0, integrated to t = 2*tau against a reference obtained by the method of steps (analytic on [0, tau], then solve_ivp at rtol = 1e-13 / atol = 1e-14): reference x(2tau) = -0.00854744434746. Halving the solver step h from 0.125 to 0.003906 gives absolute errors 2.874e-03, 7.185e-04, 1.796e-04, 4.491e-05, 1.123e-05, 2.807e-06 — an observed convergence order of 2.000, 2.000, 2.000, 2.000, 2.000. The measured order is exactly 2, not 4.
logged: No. No comment in `runge_kutta4`, `dynamics`, or `get_delayed_interpolated` states the interpolation order or the resulting order reduction, and the method's name asserts the opposite.
recommendation: This is a legitimate discretisation and the arithmetic is correct — the defect is the unstated (and name-contradicted) consistency order. Add a comment on `runge_kutta4` stating that the linear interpolation of the delayed argument in `get_delayed_interpolated` caps the global order at 2, with the measured confirmation (order 2.000 on the scalar linear test above), and either rename the method to something that does not claim order 4 or supply a cubic Hermite dense-output interpolant to recover order 4. Note additionally that `get_delayed_interpolated` performs no bounds check: the index arithmetic relies on the modulo wrap (line 43-44), which happens to be benign here because `delay_frac` is 0 exactly when `index_older` wraps onto the newest sample, but the invariant is undocumented and would break silently if the buffer sizing at env_rk_jax.py:31 ever changed.

The 'basepoint' channel is therefore re-anchored each step to a moving point, whereas Arribas' X_0 is fixed for the whole path. The docstring's justification ("its total increment is exactly X_0, which injects the absolute level") holds for a fixed window, not for a sliding one.

name: The temporal-difference difference quotient is first-order and the running reward is sampled at the wrong endpoint, with neither error stated
location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:262 (`td_error = reward + (V_next - V_t)/dt`), :693 (`total_cost += float(reward) * self.env.step_size`); src/envs/env_rk_jax.py:88 (`reward = -(final_state.x.T @ Q @ final_state.x + u.T @ R @ u)`)
claimed_object: delta = r(x(t), u(t)) - V/tau_discount + dV/dt, with dV/dt the instantaneous derivative at time t and r evaluated at time t; and J = the integral over the horizon of the running reward.
actual_behaviour: Two separate first-order inconsistencies, in opposite temporal directions. (i) dV/dt is a FORWARD (explicit Euler) difference quotient (V(t+dt) - V(t))/dt = dV/dt + O(dt), first-order accurate; the residual is anchored at the LEFT endpoint t. (ii) The reward returned by env.step is computed from `final_state.x`, i.e. x(t + dt), NOT x(t) — it is anchored at the RIGHT endpoint. So `td_error` adds r(x(t+dt), u(t)) to a derivative estimate centred at t, and the integral in `_evaluate_noiseless` (line 693) is a right-rectangle rule, also O(dt). Both are consistent as dt -> 0 and neither is wrong per se, but the mismatch of anchors means the scheme is first-order with an O(dt) bias that is not the sum of two independently-stated O(dt) terms, and nothing in the code names the order. This is entangled with, and is smaller than, the target-network lag reported separately (which contributes an O(1/dt) term, measured at 2.39x the derivative itself).
fires_in_practice: MEASURED indirectly on hopfield_nonlinear at dt = 0.1, seed 42, 3000 transitions: mean |dV/dt| (single-network forward difference) = 1.193e-01 against mean |r| = 9.458e-01, so the derivative term is roughly 13% of the reward term and the O(dt) anchor mismatch is a sub-leading but non-negligible perturbation of the residual. The magnitude of the O(dt) bias itself was NOT measured in isolation (it is masked by the target-lag term, which is an order larger).
logged: No comment in `critic_loss` states the order of the difference quotient, and no comment anywhere records that the reward is evaluated at the interval's right endpoint while the derivative is anchored at the left.
recommendation: State the order explicitly in `critic_loss`: the forward difference is O(dt) and the residual is consistent with delta as dt -> 0. Align the anchors — either evaluate the reward at x(t) (the left endpoint, matching the forward difference), or use a midpoint/trapezoidal quadrature for the running reward and a centred quotient for dV/dt to recover O(dt^2). At minimum, add the comment; an unremarked first-order scheme in an agent whose thesis rests on continuous-time fidelity is a documentation defect even where the arithmetic is defensible. Fix the target-network lag first — it dominates this by an order of magnitude.

name: discount.discounted: false silently drops the V/tau term while discount.tau remains live in the LSTD path
location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:263-264 (`if discounted: td_error = td_error - V_t/tau`), :308 (`diff = (phi_n - phi_t)/dt - phi_c/tau` — UNCONDITIONAL); conf/agent/value_gradient.yaml:29-30 (`discounted: false`, `tau: 100.0`)

That is well posed only if the closed loop is stabilised so r -> 0; on an unstable plant before the critic has learned anything, V is unbounded and the fixed point does not exist. The code never states this. The two agent paths then DISAGREE: the LSTD accumulator at line 308 applies `- phi_c/tau` UNCONDITIONALLY, ignoring `discount.discounted` altogether. So with the shipped defaults (discounted: false, tau: 100.0, lstd: false) the semi-gradient critic targets the undiscounted fixed point while the LSTD critic, selected by flipping `algorithm.lstd` to true and changing nothing else, targets the tau = 100 discounted one. Both branches were exercised in this audit (the semi-gradient probe on hopfield_nonlinear and the LSTD probe on the same cell). The NUMERICAL difference between the two fixed points was not measured.
logged: No. Nothing announces which objective is in force. `_format_progress` (line 635-637) appends a "disc" flag to the progress bar when `discounted` is true, which is the only trace — and it is absent from the metrics, the checkpoint metadata, and the LSTD path entirely.
recommendation: Make the LSTD accumulator honour `discount.discounted` so that one configuration names one objective. State in the DiscountConfig docstring what `discounted: false` means — the undiscounted infinite-horizon problem — and note that its well-posedness requires the closed loop to be stabilising, which is not guaranteed during early training on an unstable plant. Log the resolved objective (discounted with tau = ..., or undiscounted) in the startup run-context block. The current silent disagreement between two solver paths over the same YAML is the most likely source of an irreproducible comparison.

name: float32 narrowing of the initial window inside a float64 pipeline

name: JAXDDEEnv.compute_reward is dead code whose two lax.cond branches ignore the predicate's subject and differ only in sign

name: clip_action silently rewrites the control away from the greedy law, and binds on 6.0% of actions at the value shipped in signatures.yaml
location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:204-206 (do_clip guard at :197, jnp.clip at :205); the bound is conf/agent/signatures.yaml:16 (clip_action: 10.0) and conf/agent/value_gradient.yaml:14 (null)
claimed_object: u* = 1/2 R^{-1} B^T grad_{x(t)} V(x_t) — the unconstrained stationary point of the Hamiltonian r + (grad_x V)^T f, consistent with the critic, whose continuous-time TD residual delta = r - V/tau_discount + dV/dt (:263-265) is the residual of the UNCONSTRAINED HJB equation.
actual_behaviour: When clip_action is set, :205 replaces u by its componentwise projection onto the box [-clip_action, clip_action]^m. The projected control is still an argmax — R is diagonal (MEASURED: R = 0.1*I_5 on platoon_h1h2) and the Hamiltonian -x^T Q x - u^T R u + (grad_x V)^T B u is concave and separable in u, so the box-constrained maximiser IS the componentwise clip of the unconstrained one. But it is the argmax of the INPUT-CONSTRAINED optimal-control problem, whose value functional is NOT the V the critic is fitting: the critic's TD target never sees the constraint. Actor and critic therefore solve two different problems. Note the comment at :194-196 asserts the clip is unnecessary because 'for a well-initialised critic the value-gradient control law is naturally bounded (dV/dx ~ 0 at init)' — this is true only at initialisation and is contradicted by the measurement below, where the trained critic drives |u|_inf to 32.7. If R were non-diagonal the clip would not even be the constrained argmax, since the box-constrained maximiser of a non-separable concave quadratic is not the componentwise clip.
fires_in_practice: MEASURED, and it binds hard. Real ContinuousValueGradient training runs, 25 episodes, platoon_h1h2, kind=signature depth=2 (feature dim 462, window 7), instrumented by wrapping _select_action rather than editing the file: with clip_action=None (the value_gradient.yaml default) -> 7525 actions, 0 clip binds, peak |mu|_inf = 32.69, peak||x|| = 26.84. With clip_action=10.0 (the signatures.yaml value) on the identical seed and cell -> 455 of 7525 actions clipped = 6.0%, peak |mu|_inf pinned at exactly 10, and the CLOSED-LOOP TRAJECTORY CHANGES: peak||x|| falls from 26.84 to 10.68. The clip is not a safeguard on this cell; it is the controller for 6% of the rollout, and it alters the state trajectory by a factor of 2.5 in peak norm. On the other three cells measured (delayed_velocity_oscillator signature depth 3: peak |mu|_inf = 1.30; linear_dde_scalar depth 3: 0.28; double_integrator markovian degree 2: 0.11) a bound of 10.0 would not bind. Every arm of run/study/representation_study_variants.txt uses agent=value_gradient, whose clip_action is null, so the representation-study numbers are unaffected.
logged: No — completely silent. :205 is a bare jnp.clip inside a jax.jit with no counter, no warn-once, no record of how far past the bound the raw control went. The 455 binds above were only visible because _select_action was wrapped externally for this audit. This is the exact case the project rule names: a silently-active clamp regularising the very regime under study.
recommendation: Either (i) drop the clip from the value-gradient law and let the greedy control be the greedy control — the study's own configs already do this (value_gradient.yaml:14 is null, and src/envs/chemical_process.py:26-33 records a deliberate decision to run the Dadebo grid with clip_action=null precisely so the EXACT law is deployed); or (ii) if an input constraint is genuinely wanted, make it part of the MATHEMATICS: state the constrained problem, and note in the code that the critic's TD residual must then carry the constrained Hamiltonian max_{|u|<=c} [r + (grad_x V)^T f] for actor and critic to be consistent. In either case, until it is removed, instrument it per the project rule: warn once on first bind at WARNING with the raw pre-clip |u|_inf, then DEBUG with a running count and the most extreme raw value. A 6%-of-actions bind must appear in the log at default verbosity. Also correct the claim at :194-196, which the measurement falsifies.

name: divergence_threshold truncates both the episode and its reported cost, without logging

claimed_object: J = the integral over the full horizon [0, max_time] of the discounted running reward r(x(t),u(t)) = -(x^T Q x + u^T R u). Every episodic cost compared across variants must be an integral over the SAME horizon, otherwise the comparison is not of the intervention.

The accumulator at :526 (episode_cost += step_metrics.reward, with reward = r*dt at :388) then sums FEWER steps. Because r is negative-definite, a truncated episode reports a LESS NEGATIVE — i.e. apparently BETTER — cost than a completed one: divergence is rewarded in the reported metric. The truncation also shortens the LSTD accumulation (:305-314) and the TD sample count for that episode. It is NOT comfortably inert, however: on platoon_h1h2 the peak reaches 26.84, within a factor 3.7 of the 100.0 bound, on a 25-episode run at the very start of training — a longer run, a harder seed, or the 50.0 dataclass default (which would be within a factor 1.9) could plausibly cross it. The NaN test on the same line (:626-627) also never fired.

name: The DDE initial path is narrowed to float32 in a float64 pipeline, perturbing the control at the 1e-7 level
location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:163, :166, :171 (three np.asarray(..., dtype=np.float32) calls inside _fill_buffer_initial)
claimed_object: The initial condition phi of the delay differential equation, an element of C([-tau,0],R^d), sampled onto the window and represented in the pipeline's working precision. main_unified.py:63 enables jax_enable_x64; DequeBuffer's dtype is np.float64 (src/utils/dynamic_signature.py:14, and RepresentationBuffer at src/representations/factory.py:65, :73); RepresentationBuffer.append casts to that float64 dtype (factory.py:89). The pipeline is float64 throughout.
actual_behaviour: _fill_buffer_initial appends the initial path's taps as float32. DequeBuffer.to_array (dynamic_signature.py:30) then widens them back to float64, so the loss is silent and irreversible: the float64 window is populated with float32-rounded values. The precision is INCONSISTENT within one window — the initial-path taps carry float32 round-off while every tap appended during the episode (via :352 -> factory.py:89) carries full float64 — so the discretised phi and its continuation are not represented in the same precision. This is code-review finding F-E1 (commits 07b8d4a, 7b1153e) surviving in _fill_buffer_initial; the same narrowing exists at src/agents/CSAC_jax.py:326.
classification: B CHANGES-THE-ANSWER (small but non-zero, and silent)
fires_in_practice: MEASURED, on every episode reset of every run, with a visible effect on the control. In the CARE test on the markovian double integrator with the critic set to the exact V(x) = -x^T P x: for x0 = (0.3, -1.7) the window endpoint comes back as [0.30000001, -1.70000005] instead of [0.3, -1.7], and the resulting control is u_code = 2.64448644 against u_care = 2.64448637, a ratio of 1.00000003 — a relative control error of 3e-8, i.e. float32 epsilon. The two exactly-representable test points ((1,1) and (-2,0.5)) gave ratio 1.000000 exactly, which is what confirms the 3e-8 is the narrowing and not the CARE solve. The error propagates: it enters grad_path[-1] and hence every control of the episode's opening steps, and it enters sig_t of the first TD update.
logged: No, and it is invisible by construction: to_array widens back to float64, so downstream dtype checks all pass and nothing indicates the values ever left float64.
recommendation: Use the buffer's own dtype at all three sites: np.asarray(x/self.training.scale, dtype=self.sliding_signature.dtype) — RepresentationBuffer already exposes .dtype (factory.py:72), so no new constant is needed. This makes _fill_buffer_initial consistent with append (factory.py:89) and with the jax_enable_x64 pipeline, and the CARE test must then return ratio 1.000000 for (0.3,-1.7) as it already does for the exactly-representable points. If float32 is ever wanted for a precision-comparison study, it must be selected through the existing dtype parameter, not hard-coded. Apply the same fix at CSAC_jax.py:326.
severity: Low in magnitude (3e-8 relative, MEASURED), but it is a silent precision truncation on the DDE's initial condition — the very object the parallel workflow is being fixed to load correctly — and it costs one word per line to remove.

name: The history window is over-long by 3 taps, from an undocumented constant, and the mathematical window is exactly [-tau, 0]
location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:60-62 (_compute_window_size: int(np.ceil(max_delay / self.env.step_size)) + 3 if max_delay > 0 else 10), consumed at :56-57 and :86
claimed_object: The functional state x_t : s -> x(t+s), s in [-tau, 0] — a path on an interval of length EXACTLY tau. Its minimal uniform discretisation at the control cadence dt is K+1 samples spanning K*dt >= tau, with K = ceil(tau/dt).
actual_behaviour: window_size = K+3, and window_length = window_size + 1 = K+4 (:86), so the window holds K+4 samples spanning (K+3)*dt — three taps and 3*dt of time MORE than [-tau,0]. Two distinct consequences. (a) The window is a strict superset of x_t: it includes states strictly older than the delay, which the DDE's right-hand side (env_rk_jax.py:51) cannot depend on. The value functional's class is not thereby reduced (V(x_t) remains representable), but the feature dimension and the conditioning both grow for nothing. (b) At episode start the three extra taps are not data at all: the padding branch (:165-172) fills them by CONSTANT-REPEATING subsampled[0] = phi(-tau), fabricating a stationary prefix that is not part of phi. That prefix is not signature-inert: the time-augmentation channel (dynamic_signature.py:206, jnp.linspace(0.0, time_origin, n)) advances across it while the state stays constant, so the time-state mixed signature terms differ from those of the true phi. The two agents disagree: signatures_jax.py:163 uses ceil(max_delay/step_size) + 1, i.e. one extra tap, not three. Neither 3 nor 1 is justified anywhere; `git log -S` traces the +3 to the initial import commit a02cc92 with no rationale.
classification: D DISCRETISATION (legitimate in kind — the window must be sampled — but the arithmetic is unjustified and inconsistent between agents)
fires_in_practice: MEASURED on every delayed run, and the over-length is large. Instantiating all 22 shipped env configs through Hydra and computing (K+3)*dt / tau: MG_1D_chaotic 1.044 (tau=17, dt=0.25, K=68), MG_1D 1.176, MG_1D_limit_cycle 1.125 (tau=6, dt=0.25, K=24), chemical_reaction_4D 1.150, delay_jax 1.150 (tau=1, dt=0.05, K=20), delay_jax_unstable 1.300, unstable_oscillator_delay 1.231, platoon_5car 1.300, strongly_delayed_oscillator 1.300, delayed_velocity_oscillator 1.500 (tau=0.3, dt=0.05, K=6), hopfield_linear / hopfield_nonlinear / hopfield_duffing 1.600 (tau=0.5, dt=0.1, K=5), linear_dde_scalar 1.600 (tau=1.0, dt=0.2, K=5), delayed_oscillator_high_gap 1.750 and platoon_h1h2 1.750 (tau=0.2, dt=0.05, K=4). So on the two H1/H2 cells with the coarsest delay resolution the window is 75% longer than the delay, and 3 of its 8 taps lie outside [-tau,0]. Confirmed against a live agent: platoon_h1h2 -> window_size=7 (K=4), feature dim 462; delayed_velocity_oscillator -> window_size=9 (K=6), feature dim 155.
logged: No. The derived window_size silently overwrites the configured one at :56-57 (documents/methodology/code_review.md F-C2 records this same silent override), so conf/agent/value_gradient.yaml:49's window_size: 40 is discarded without a message. The signature agent at least prints its override (signatures_jax.py:167); the value-gradient agent does not.
recommendation: Set window_size = ceil(max_delay/step_size), giving window_length = K+1 samples spanning K*dt >= tau — the minimal uniform grid covering [-tau,0] exactly — and add a comment stating that K*dt >= tau with equality when tau/dt is an integer (true for all 22 shipped configs, measured), and that the residual (K*dt - tau) is the O(dt) discretisation slack. Re-run one representation-study arm before and after to record the change in feature dimension and cost. If the extra taps are wanted for a reason (a numerical-differentiation stencil at the endpoint, say), state that reason in the code — 3 is currently a magic number that disagrees with the other agent's magic number 1. Also print the derived window_size, as signatures_jax.py:167 does, so a run's log states the window actually used.
severity: Medium — legitimate in kind and not wrong in the sense of losing information, but the window is up to 1.75x the mathematical object, the constant is unjustified, the two agents disagree, and the episode-start padding fabricates path data outside phi's domain.

name: The initial window's endpoint is not guaranteed to be x(t0): the history is strided from the OLDEST sample, so the endpoint survives only by an arithmetic coincidence
location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:157 (subsampled = history_data[::self.env.resolution]), consumed at :160-172; the source array is src/envs/env_rk_jax.py:176-193 (JAXEnvWrapper.initial_conditions)
claimed_object: The window's last tap must be x(t), so that grad_path[-1] (:203) is the derivative with respect to the ENDPOINT — Dupire's vertical derivative — which is what the control law u = 1/2 R^{-1} B^T grad_{x(t)} V requires. The window's taps must also be uniformly spaced at the control cadence dt, because the feature map's time channel is a uniform grid (dynamic_signature.py:206, jnp.linspace).
actual_behaviour: initial_conditions returns the solver-cadence history at spacing solver_step_size = step_size/resolution, ordered oldest-first with ordered_data[-1] = x(t0). Line 157 strides it FORWARD from index 0, so the taps retained are indices 0, resolution, 2*resolution, ... and the last one retained is resolution*floor((capacity-1)/resolution). This equals capacity-1 — i.e. the endpoint x(t0) is retained — if and only if (capacity-1) % resolution == 0, where capacity = ceil(tau/solver_step_size) + 1 (env_rk_jax.py:31). When the condition fails, buffer[-1] is a PAST sample of phi, grad_path[-1] is the derivative with respect to that past sample rather than the endpoint, and the control law is differentiating the wrong coordinate. A second consequence: the whole retained prefix sits at times offset from the multiples of dt, so once the episode's own appends (at exact multiples of dt from t0) begin, the window's taps are NON-UNIFORMLY spaced — there is a gap of a fraction of dt between the pre-reset chunk and the first post-reset sample — while the feature map's linspace time channel assumes uniform spacing. That inconsistency persists for window_length steps, until the initial taps slide out.
classification: C WRONG-OBJECT (latent: the condition holds for every shipped config, measured)
fires_in_practice: MEASURED on both sides. It does NOT fire on any shipped configuration: instantiating all 22 env configs and evaluating (capacity-1) % resolution gives 0 for every delayed cell — MG_1D (cap 86, res 5), MG_1D_chaotic (341, 5), MG_1D_limit_cycle (121, 5), chemical_reaction_4D (81, 4), delay_jax (121, 6), delay_jax_unstable (41, 4), delayed_oscillator_high_gap (17, 4), delayed_velocity_oscillator (25, 4), hopfield_linear / hopfield_nonlinear / hopfield_duffing (21, 4), linear_dde_scalar (21, 4), platoon_5car (41, 4), platoon_h1h2 (17, 4), strongly_delayed_oscillator (41, 4), unstable_oscillator_delay (66, 5). The reason is that tau/step_size happens to be an exact integer in every shipped cell, which forces capacity-1 = (tau/dt)*resolution. It DOES fire on a constructed config: with tau=0.35, dt=0.1, resolution=4 (capacity=15, (15-1)%4 = 2) and a non-constant initial path phi(s) = (s, s^2) passed as history_function, buffer[-1] comes back as [-0.05, 0.0025] = phi(-dt/2) instead of phi(0) = [0, 0] — the endpoint is MISSED and a past sample is differentiated. The same was reproduced at tau=0.5, dt=0.2, resolution=4 (capacity 11, remainder 2), where buffer[-1] = [-0.1, 0.01] instead of [0, 0]. So the correctness of the vertical derivative at episode start currently rests on an unstated arithmetic coincidence about tau/dt, in a codebase whose configs are edited by hand.
logged: No — there is no assertion, no check, and no message. A config with a non-integer tau/dt would silently differentiate the wrong coordinate on the opening steps of every episode and nothing would indicate it.
recommendation: Stride from the ENDPOINT, not from the start: subsampled = history_data[::-1][::self.env.resolution][::-1], which retains x(t0) unconditionally and lands the taps on exact multiples of dt back from t0, restoring uniform spacing. Add the assertion that makes the invariant explicit and self-documenting: assert np.allclose(subsampled[-1], history_data[-1]), with a comment stating that buffer[-1] must be x(t) because :203 differentiates it as the window endpoint. A cheap regression test: reset with a non-constant history_function and check buffer[-1] == phi(0) for a config with (capacity-1) % resolution != 0.
severity: Medium — dormant on every shipped config (measured), but it is the vertical derivative itself that breaks, silently, and only an unstated coincidence about tau/dt is holding it up.

name: noise.smooth claims a smooth Gaussian-process exploration path but computes white noise to machine precision at the shipped length_scale
location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:410-447 (_on_episode_start GP construction; kernel at :425, Cholesky jitter at :428, sample at :443-446); the length scale is conf/agent/value_gradient.yaml:40 (0.002) against src/configs.py:66 (default 0.2)
claimed_object: A temporally correlated exploration signal: the code's own comment at :412-413 states 'Kernel: Squared Exponential (RBF): k(t, t') = sigma^2 * exp(-|t-t'|^2 / (2 * l^2))', i.e. a GP path whose correlation length is noise.length_scale. Smooth exploration is the mathematically motivated choice for a functional/delay plant, where a white control signal makes u a discontinuous forcing of the DDE and the window sees no coherent excitation.
actual_behaviour: The kernel is evaluated on the CONTROL grid ts = np.arange(0, max_time + 5*step_size, step_size) (:416), so the relevant quantity is the correlation between ADJACENT grid points, exp(-dt^2/(2*l^2)). At the shipped length_scale = 0.002 and dt in {0.05, 0.25} this is zero to machine precision: K is the identity matrix, its Cholesky factor is the identity, and :446 returns i.i.d. Gaussians scaled by sigma. The 341x341 covariance matrix, the Cholesky decomposition, the SVD fallback (:433-438) and the 1e-6 jitter (:428) are all computed to produce, exactly, white noise. The configured object (a smooth path) and the computed object (white noise) differ, and the config reads as though the former were in use.
fires_in_practice: MEASURED, on every episode of every run with noise.smooth: true (which is the shipped value_gradient.yaml:39). Analytically, exp(-dt^2/(2*l^2)) at l = 0.002: dt = 0.05 -> 1.918556e-136; dt = 0.25 -> 0.000000e+00 exactly. Empirically, rebuilding the agent's exact construction (same ts grid, same K, same 1e-6 jitter, same Cholesky, same jax.random.normal) and measuring the lag-1 autocorrelation of the realised sample: l = 0.002, dt = 0.05 -> -0.0864 (white noise, as the finite-sample scatter about 0 confirms); l = 0.2, dt = 0.05 -> +0.9799 (genuinely smooth, which is what the configs.py default 0.2 would deliver). So the shipped 0.002 defeats the feature by two orders of magnitude in l. Consequence for the 1e-6 Cholesky jitter at :428: it is INERT, but only because K is already the identity — it is inert for the wrong reason, and would cease to be inert the moment length_scale is corrected. Also observed while reading (NOT separately measured): the GP is sampled at :446 with self._sigma_effective, which _on_episode_start reads BEFORE _select_action has run for the new episode, so under schedule='linear_decay' or 'adaptive' episode k's noise path is scaled by the sigma left over from the last step of episode k-1. Under the shipped schedule='constant' (value_gradient.yaml:37) this is inert.
logged: No. Nothing reports the realised correlation, and nothing warns that length_scale << step_size makes the GP degenerate. The Cholesky has a print at :435, but only on the LinAlgError fallback, which cannot trigger when K is the identity.
recommendation: Decide which object is wanted and make the code compute it. If smooth exploration is intended, set noise.length_scale to a few multiples of the control step (l >= 3*step_size gives lag-1 correlation >= 0.99, and l = 0.2 at dt = 0.05 was measured to give 0.9799), and add a guard at :425 warning when length_scale < step_size that the kernel is numerically diagonal and the sample is white. If white exploration is intended, set noise.smooth: false and delete the O(n^2) GP machinery from the hot path — it currently costs a 341x341 Cholesky per episode to produce what jax.random.normal produces for free at :246. Either way the comment at :412-413 must describe what is computed. While there, fix the sigma staleness at :446 by computing _sigma_effective for the incoming episode before sampling.
severity: Medium — the exploration signal is not the object the config names, on every shipped value-gradient run; it does not corrupt the reported cost directly (exploration noise is not the measured quantity), but the whole point of smooth exploration on a delay plant is to excite the history window coherently, and that is not happening.

name: The DDE's initial condition is sampled as a POINT: the sampler's support is the constant paths, a measure-zero subset of C([-tau,0],R^d), and no history_function is ever passed
location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:138-141 (_sample_initial_state) and :500-501 (wrapper.reset with x0 only, history_function omitted); the constant extension happens at src/envs/env_rk_jax.py:77 (data_history = jnp.tile(self.x0, (self.buffer_size, 1)))
claimed_object: The initial condition of a controlled delay differential equation xdot(t) = f(x_t) + g(x_t) u(t) is a PATH phi in C([-tau,0],R^d) — an infinite-dimensional object. Training a value FUNCTIONAL V(x_t) on path space requires the initial-condition distribution to charge that space; this is the same mathematical point the parallel workflow is fixing on the actor-critic's preheat, and the agent's own comment at :504-509 asserts it ('The DDE initial condition is the initial PATH phi on [-tau, 0], already loaded into the signature window by _fill_buffer_initial() from the env history buffer').
actual_behaviour: _sample_initial_state returns jax.random.normal(subkey, shape=(self.env.N,)) — a POINT in R^d, not a path. :500-501 then calls self.wrapper.reset(subkey, x0=np.array(x_init), t0=0.0) WITHOUT the history_function argument, so JAXDDEEnv.reset takes the else branch at env_rk_jax.py:76-77 and fills the entire history buffer with jnp.tile(x0, (buffer_size, 1)) — the CONSTANT path phi(s) = x0 for all s in [-tau,0]. The comment at :504-509 is therefore accurate about the mechanism (the window IS loaded from the env history rather than by a zero-control burn-in — that fix is in place) but the phi so loaded is drawn from a d-dimensional submanifold of constant paths, not from path space. JAXDDEEnv.reset DOES accept a history_function and vmaps it over the correct time grid (env_rk_jax.py:71-75), and JAXEnvWrapper.reset forwards it (env_rk_jax.py:116-126) — the capability exists and is fully wired; the agent simply never uses it. Grepping the agent for history_function returns nothing.
fires_in_practice: MEASURED, in two parts. (a) The mechanism is confirmed by execution: resetting with history_function=None and inspecting wrapper.initial_conditions returns a history whose every row equals x0 — the constant path. Passing a non-constant history_function phi(s) = (s, s^2) DOES populate the window with the true non-constant path (verified across six delay configurations, where the window's first taps come back as phi(-tau) = (-0.3, 0.09) for tau=0.3, (-17, 289) for tau=17, etc.), which proves the path capability works and only the agent's call site is deficient. (b) The sampler is dormant on the shipped config: conf/agent/value_gradient.yaml:71 sets fix_initial_state: true, so :492-493 takes the else branch and x_init = self.x0 every episode. The consequence is arguably worse than the sampler being wrong — the ENTIRE training distribution is then the SINGLE constant path phi(s) = x0, and V is fitted on a one-point subset of path space while being evaluated as a functional on it. Every run measured for this audit trained from that single constant path.
logged: No. Nothing states that the initial condition is a constant path rather than a sampled path, and the comment at :504-509 reads as though a genuine phi were being loaded — which is true of the MECHANISM but not of the DISTRIBUTION.
recommendation: Make _sample_initial_state return a PATH and pass it: sample phi from a path measure on C([-tau,0],R^d) — a Gaussian process on [-tau,0] with a correlation length comparable to tau, or a random truncated Fourier series, or (cheapest and already available) the free evolution of the plant from a random point, which lies on the plant's own attractor and is the natural measure — then hand it to wrapper.reset(..., history_function=phi) at :500-501, which already accepts it (env_rk_jax.py:116) and vmaps it onto the correct grid (env_rk_jax.py:71-75). The window is then filled by _fill_buffer_initial from the true phi with no other change, and the F4 endpoint fix above becomes load-bearing (with a constant phi the stride bug is invisible; with a genuine phi it is not — which is exactly how it was surfaced for this audit). Whatever is chosen, the comment at :504-509 must say WHICH measure on path space is being sampled, and the constant-path case must be named as such rather than left implicit. Separately, reconsider fix_initial_state: true: fitting a functional on path space from one point of that space is the more consequential half of this finding.
severity: Medium — the same class of defect as the preheat the owner objected to (a point standing in for a path), in the same agent, on the same object; dormant as a SAMPLER on the shipped config only because the shipped config collapses the distribution to a single constant path, which is not an improvement.

name: A silent substitution of the TD time step by an unrelated magic constant, presented as a division guard
location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:348-349 (if dt <= 1e-9: dt = 1e-4); the identical construction is at src/agents/base_jax.py:243-244
claimed_object: dt, the control-cadence time step, is the discretisation parameter of the continuous-time TD residual delta = r - V/tau_discount + dV/dt, which the code forms as reward + (V_next - V_t)/dt at :263. It must be the ACTUAL interval between sig_t and sig_next, otherwise the residual is not the residual of the HJB equation.
actual_behaviour: If dt <= 1e-9 the code replaces it by 1e-4 — a value FIVE ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE larger than the threshold that triggers the replacement. This is not a floor and not an epsilon: a floor would clamp to 1e-9. Were it ever to fire, (V_next - V_t)/dt would be computed with a denominator wrong by up to 1e5, the TD residual would be silently falsified, and the loss (:266, scaled by dt) and the effective learning rate (:104, critic_lr * step_size) would be inconsistent with it. dt is read from self.env.step_size, a config constant that cannot become small at runtime, so the guard is protecting against a condition that a configuration error would cause and that an assertion should catch loudly.
classification: A INERT (provably: no shipped config comes within seven orders of magnitude of the threshold) — but it is not commented as inert, and the project rule requires exactly that comment
fires_in_practice: MEASURED, cannot fire on any shipped configuration. Instantiating all 22 env configs gives step_size in {0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.25, 1.0}; the minimum is 0.01 (harmonic_oscillator, stable_non_normal_2D, unstable_2D_env, chemical_reaction_4D), which exceeds the 1e-9 threshold by seven orders of magnitude. The branch is dead code on every shipped cell. It was also never taken in any of the four real training runs measured for this audit (~20 500 steps).
logged: No, and the comment '# Avoid division by zero' actively misleads: it describes a floor, whereas the code performs a substitution by an unrelated constant. A reader auditing for silent truncations would classify this line as benign on the strength of that comment.
recommendation: Replace with an assertion at construction time, where the invariant belongs: assert self.env.step_size > 0, f'step_size must be positive, got {self.env.step_size}' in _init_env. This fails loudly on the configuration error the guard is imagining, costs nothing in the hot path, and removes a line that silently falsifies the TD residual if the impossible ever happens. If the branch is kept, the project rule applies verbatim — it must carry a comment stating why it is inert (min shipped step_size = 0.01, threshold 1e-9) and it must not substitute 1e-4 for a quantity it has just declared to be below 1e-9. Same treatment at base_jax.py:243-244.
severity: Low — provably dead on every shipped config, but it is a silent substitution mis-labelled as a division guard, and the project rule is explicit that only a provably-inert clamp may go unlogged and only with a comment stating why.

name: signature.time_origin and signature.state_augmentation are dead parameters in the value-gradient path

name: The running reward is evaluated at the step's right endpoint while the TD residual pairs it with a forward difference
location: src/envs/env_rk_jax.py:88 (reward = -(final_state.x.T @ self.Q @ final_state.x + u.T @ self.R @ u)); consumed at src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:263 (td_error = reward + (V_next - V_t) / dt) and accumulated at :388, :526
claimed_object: J = the integral of the discounted running reward r(x(t), u(t)) = -(x^T Q x + u^T R u), and the continuous-time TD residual delta = r(x(t),u(t)) - V(x_t)/tau_discount + (d/dt)V(x_t), in which r and dV/dt are evaluated at the SAME instant t.
actual_behaviour: env.step advances the plant by `resolution` solver sub-steps and returns the reward evaluated at final_state.x = x(t+dt), the RIGHT endpoint, with u held at its zero-order-hold value over [t, t+dt]. Line 263 then adds this r(x(t+dt), u(t)) to the FORWARD difference (V(x_{t+dt}) - V(x_t))/dt, which approximates dV/dt at the LEFT endpoint t. The two terms of the residual are therefore anchored at opposite ends of the step. Both are first-order accurate, so delta is consistent and the scheme converges as dt -> 0 — this is a legitimate discretisation, not an error — but the pairing is a right-rectangle rule against a forward difference rather than a matched pair, and the episodic cost at :388/:526 is correspondingly a right Riemann sum of r, not the left-endpoint sum the running-cost notation r(x(t),u(t)) suggests. Nothing states the convention or its order.
classification: D DISCRETISATION (consistent, first-order; the arithmetic is right but the convention is unstated)
fires_in_practice: MEASURED, on every step of every run — it is the definition of the reward, not a branch. The magnitude of the mismatch is O(dt) relative and is therefore largest on the coarsest cells: step_size = 1.0 on MG_1D and 0.25 on MG_1D_chaotic / MG_1D_limit_cycle (both measured from the instantiated configs), against 0.01 on the finest. The MG_1D_limit_cycle config comment (conf/env/MG_1D_limit_cycle.yaml:16) already identifies step_size as 'the sole conditioning lever (dt=1 diverges)', so the O(dt) terms on these cells are known to be non-negligible. The separate consequence — that episode truncation by divergence_threshold makes the cost a sum over a variable number of steps — is finding F6 above.
logged: No. Neither the convention (right endpoint) nor its order (first-order) is stated at env_rk_jax.py:88 or at value_gradient_jax.py:263, and the docstrings write the running cost as r(x(t), u(t)), which is the left-endpoint object.
recommendation: No behavioural change is required — the scheme is consistent. State the convention where it is defined: a comment at env_rk_jax.py:88 recording that r is evaluated at x(t+dt) with u held constant over [t, t+dt], and a comment at value_gradient_jax.py:263 recording that this right-endpoint r is paired with a forward difference of V, so delta = delta_exact + O(dt) as dt -> 0, and that the episodic cost is accordingly a right Riemann sum. If a matched pair is wanted at no cost, evaluate the reward at state.x (the left endpoint) instead of final_state.x, which pairs the left-endpoint r with the forward difference; the change is one identifier, and its effect should be measured on the coarsest cell (MG_1D at dt=1.0) before adoption. The project rule on stating convergence/consistency for a necessary discretisation applies here: the arithmetic is right, and only the statement is missing.
severity: Low — consistent and first-order accurate, so no reported number is wrong; but the convention is unstated on cells where the config's own comments identify dt as the dominant conditioning lever.

name: training.divergence_threshold — silent episode truncation
location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:628 (also src/agents/signatures_jax.py:456, src/agents/CSAC_jax.py:634)

The accumulated reward stops there, so the reported cost is an integral over a strictly shorter, state-dependent interval [0, t_cut] with t_cut < max_time. A divergent episode is thereby assigned a finite, small-magnitude cost that is arithmetically comparable to a completed episode's but is not the same functional. No print, warning or metric records that the cut occurred, nor at what episode, step or ||x||.
fires_in_practice: MEASURED. Instrumented runs of ContinuousValueGradient (hydra-composed, agent=value_gradient, divergence_threshold=100.0). FIRES: env=strongly_delayed_oscillator — 20/20 episodes truncated, ||x|| at the cut 101.5/104.5/101.8/102.7/105.2, episodes completed only 0.363-0.390 of the 300-step horizon, reported cost_episodic = -4749.209, -5643.003 for the first two episodes; env=unstable_2D_env — 30/30 episodes truncated, first cuts at ||x||=100.31, 100.34, 100.80, peak ||x||=inf. logged: No. The truncation is entirely silent at every level; no WARNING, no DEBUG, no metric. A reader of figure_training_metrics.png cannot distinguish a truncated episode from a completed one.
recommendation: Log the first activation at WARNING (episode, step, ||x||, threshold) and subsequent ones at DEBUG, per the project clamp rule. Record a per-episode truncation flag and the achieved horizon t_cut alongside cost_episodic, so a truncated episode is never plotted against, or averaged with, a completed one. Mathematically the cleaner alternative is to keep the guard as a numerical-overflow stop only and report the episode as cost = +infinity (divergent), which is the true value of the functional, rather than a finite truncated integral.

name: np.linalg.lstsq(..., rcond=None) — silent truncated-SVD on the H1/H2 least-squares fit
location: run/study/h1h2_evaluation.py:378 (also run/study/mwe_e0_nn_critic.py:158, run/study/diagnose_optimization_floor.py:88, run/study/mwe_real_platoon_offmanifold_cheat.py:171)
claimed_object: The plain least-squares value fit theta = argmin ||Phi theta - V*||^2 over the full feature span, described in the code comment as '0 = plain lstsq' (the unregularised baseline against which the H1H2_RIDGE option is contrasted).
actual_behaviour: numpy's `rcond=None` is NOT 'no cutoff'; it selects the default cutoff max(M,N)*eps ~ 4e-13 relative, i.e. a truncated-SVD estimator that discards every singular direction below that threshold. The solve is therefore a rank-truncated regularised estimator, not the plain least-squares solution, and the truncation is data-dependent: it fires on the signature arm (whose design matrix is near-rank-deficient by construction, e.g. through the shuffle identity S^{ij}+S^{ji} = S^i S^j) and not on the Markovian arm. The contender of the hypothesis under test is thus the only arm being silently regularised.
fires_in_practice: MEASURED. Singular-value spectra of the actual design matrices (seed 0, on_off_sheet, n_off=500), cutoff = max(M,N)*eps*s_max: cell markovian — markovian rank 5/5 (cond 8.0e0), raw_history 65/65 (cond 1.1e2), signature 22/30 TRUNCATED, 8 directions discarded (cond 4.476e17); cell linear_dde — markovian 2/2, raw_history 27/27, signature 8/12 TRUNCATED, 4 discarded (cond 1.913e17); cell hopfield_linear — markovian 5/5, raw_history 90/90, signature 29/30 TRUNCATED, 1 discarded (cond 2.856e14); cell platoon — markovian 65/65, raw_history 946/1325 TRUNCATED (379 discarded, cond 4.827e16), signature 386/462 TRUNCATED (76 discarded, cond 2.976e19). Effect on the REPORTED closed-loop cost, measured by re-solving with rcond=-1 (no truncation) and re-rolling: cell linear_dde signature I_cl 0.192588 (shipped) vs 0.192889 (untruncated), 1.6e-3 relative, cos 0.928603 unchanged to 6 digits; cell hopfield_linear signature I_cl 0.108379 vs 0.108384 (4.6e-5 relative), cos 0.942021 vs 0.941960. Markovian and raw_history arms bit-identical under both settings on both cells. The measured shift is one to two orders below the MARGIN=0.03 that decides the printed H2 verdict on the two cells measured; NOT MEASURED on platoon and mg_chaotic, where 76-379 directions are discarded and the shift could be larger.
logged: No. The numerical rank, the cutoff and the number of discarded directions are never printed or stored; summary.json records only dim, r2, cos and I.
recommendation: Make the estimator an explicit, stated choice rather than a numpy default: pass an explicit rcond, record the numerical rank and the discarded-direction count of every arm in summary.json, and print a WARNING when rank < dim. State in the methodology that the signature design matrix is exactly rank-deficient (shuffle relations), so that the truncation is understood as a necessary projection onto the realisable span (class D) rather than an incidental regulariser — and verify the effect on the platoon and mg_chaotic cells before any H2 verdict is quoted from them.

name: 'Smooth GP exploration' is white noise at the shipped length scale
location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:404-434 (K construction, jitter, Cholesky); conf/agent/value_gradient.yaml:39 (length_scale: 0.002)
claimed_object: Temporally-correlated exploration: a Gaussian-process path with squared-exponential kernel k(t,t') = sigma^2 exp(-|t-t'|^2/(2 l^2)), documented in run/study/trick_ablation_variants.txt as 'core Doya machinery ... NOT ablated (it is not a trick)' precisely because 'i.i.d. per-step noise has the wrong continuous limit (its trajectory effect ~sqrt(dt) -> 0)'.
actual_behaviour: The kernel is evaluated on the control grid t_k = k*dt with l = 0.002, so the nearest-neighbour correlation is exp(-dt^2/(2 l^2)), which underflows to zero for every shipped dt. The covariance matrix is numerically the identity, its Cholesky factor is 1.0000005*I (the 1e-6 jitter being the only off-unit content), and the sampled 'GP path' is i.i.d. Gaussian — exactly the object the ablation rationale says must not be used. The noise.smooth flag therefore does not select the mathematical object it claims to.
fires_in_practice: MEASURED. K[i,i+1] = exp(-dt^2/(2 l^2)): 3.727e-06 at dt=0.01, l=0.002 (stable_non_normal_2D, the trick-ablation cell); 1.919e-136 at dt=0.05 (delayed_oscillator_high_gap); exactly 0.000e+00 at dt=0.25 (MG_1D_limit_cycle); 4.394e-02 at dt=0.05, l=0.02 (the signatures.yaml agent). Cholesky factor: max off-diagonal 3.7e-06 / 1.9e-136 / 0.0, diagonal mean 1.000000500. Sampled lag-1 autocorrelation of the generated 'smooth' noise: -0.0340 / -0.0864 / -0.0640 — statistically indistinguishable from white. Corroborated by the repository's own reported artefact data/main_unified/trick_ablation_convergence/ablation_convergence.json: variant 'baseline' (smooth=true) final_rho_mean 0.03636 +/- 0.0034 versus variant 'white_noise' (smooth=false) 0.03662 +/- 0.0034 and both at episodes_to_threshold 190 — the two arms of that contrast are the same noise law up to the RNG stream, so the ablation as reported does not test what its rationale states.
logged: No. Nothing reports the realised correlation length, and the flag noise.smooth=true reads as if the GP were active.
recommendation: Set length_scale to a genuine multiple of dt (correlation time l >> dt is required for the GP path to be a smooth control perturbation with an O(1) trajectory effect); at minimum, assert at construction that exp(-dt^2/(2 l^2)) exceeds a stated floor and log the realised lag-1 correlation in the run context. The trick-ablation baseline-versus-white_noise contrast must be re-run once the kernel is correlated, since as reported it compares white noise to white noise.

name: LSTD Tikhonov regulariser — two incompatible conventions, and a silent non-finite skip
location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:727 (`Mk + self._lstd_reg * abs(scale) * np.eye(rank)`, relative), 734 (`self._lstd_M + self._lstd_reg * np.eye(d)`, absolute), 739 (`if np.all(np.isfinite(theta))`)
claimed_object: The continuous-time temporal-difference fixed point E[phi delta] = 0, solved as theta = -(M)^{-1} b, with reg a small perturbation whose effect vanishes as reg -> 0.
actual_behaviour: Three distinct issues. (i) The full-dimensional branch adds an ABSOLUTE ridge reg*I to M, whose entries scale as (feature scale)^2/dt — so the same lstd_reg=1e-3 means a different amount of regularisation on every cell and at every dt; the truncated-rank branch instead adds a RELATIVE ridge reg*|trace(Mk)/rank|*I. The two branches implement different estimators under one configuration name, and the project memory records that the absolute ridge M + reg*I is NON-MONOTONIC in reg on this problem, so 'small reg' does not imply 'small effect'. (ii) M is not symmetric positive semi-definite (it is a sum of outer products phi_c diff^T with diff not proportional to phi_c), so reg*I is not a well-posed Tikhonov regulariser on it at all — it shifts a non-symmetric spectrum. (iii) `if np.all(np.isfinite(theta))` silently declines to write the critic when the solve returns a non-finite parameter, leaving the previous episode's critic in place with no record.
fires_in_practice: NOT MEASURED — and it cannot fire on any currently reported run: `lstd: false` in conf/agent/value_gradient.yaml and a grep across conf/ and run/ finds no config or study variant setting lstd=true, lstd_rank or lstd_reg. The three defects are latent, not active. The finding is recorded because the option is documented in the config as the recommended remedy 'stable where semi-gradient TD diverges', so it is likely to be switched on.
logged: No. Neither the realised ridge magnitude relative to ||M||, nor the discarded rank, nor the non-finite skip is reported.
recommendation: Before lstd is enabled for any reported result: unify the two branches on the relative (scale-aware) convention so lstd_reg has one meaning; log reg*||I||/||M|| and the solve's residual each episode; raise, do not silently skip, on a non-finite theta; and, given the recorded non-monotonicity in reg, report a reg-sweep alongside any LSTD number rather than a single value.

name: jnp.clip(noise_scale, 0.1, 1.0) in the adaptive noise schedule — dead in the configs, live in the defaults
location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:223 (`noise_scale = jnp.clip((V_TARGET - V_t)/(V_TARGET - V_BAD + 1e-6), 0.1, 1.0)`); default set at src/configs.py:63 and src/configs.py:198
claimed_object: The exploration noise amplitude sigma of the stochastic control perturbation.
actual_behaviour: In the 'adaptive' branch the noise amplitude is a value-dependent factor floored at 0.1 and ceiled at 1.0, with a 1e-6 added to the denominator. Both bounds and the epsilon act silently. The branch is unreachable under the shipped configs, but NoiseConfig.schedule defaults to 'adaptive' (configs.py:63) and from_legacy_params defaults to 'adaptive' (configs.py:198), so any agent constructed without an explicit noise block — which is exactly what a new study script or a unit test does — silently gets the clipped value-dependent schedule instead of the constant sigma used by every reported run.
fires_in_practice: MEASURED not to fire on any shipped configuration: every agent config in conf/agent/ (base_jax, value_gradient, CTAC_sig_MG_1D, CTAC_sig_chemical, CTAC_jax, signatures) sets `schedule: constant`, and no study variant file overrides it; the adaptive branch is therefore never entered on any reported run. The clip's activation rate under the adaptive schedule is not measured.
logged: No.
recommendation: Change the dataclass default from 'adaptive' to 'constant' so the default object matches the one every reported run uses, and so a config-less construction cannot silently enable a clipped schedule. If the adaptive schedule is retained, log the clip's activation and the pre-clip factor.

name: dt <= 1e-9 -> dt = 1e-4 division guard
location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:348-349 (`if dt <= 1e-9: dt = 1e-4  # Avoid division by zero`)
claimed_object: The temporal-difference step dt appearing in delta = r - V/tau_discount + (V_next - V_t)/dt and in the loss weight 0.5*delta^2*dt.
actual_behaviour: If the step were below 1e-9 the guard would replace it by 1e-4 — a factor of at least 1e5 change in the temporal-difference denominator, silently. It cannot fire, because dt is bound to env.step_size, a configuration constant, immediately above (line 345).
fires_in_practice: MEASURED not to fire, and provably cannot: dt = self.env.step_size is a config constant and the minimum over every file in conf/env/ is 0.01 (the full set of shipped values is {0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.25, 1}), all seven orders above the 1e-9 trigger. A run would have to configure step_size <= 1e-9, which would be unusable for other reasons.
logged: No — permissible for an inert clamp, but the project rule requires a comment saying why it is inert, and the present comment ('Avoid division by zero') states the intent, not the inertness argument.
recommendation: Either delete the guard (dt is a validated configuration constant, not a runtime quantity, so the correct place to reject a degenerate step is a config assertion at construction) or keep it and replace the comment with the inertness argument: dt = env.step_size is a config constant with a minimum of 0.01 across conf/env, so the branch is unreachable. A silent factor-1e5 substitution of the temporal-difference denominator is not something to leave behind an unargued comment.

name: Cholesky jitter K += 1e-6 * I on the exploration-noise covariance
location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:428 (`K += 1e-6 * np.eye(n_points)`)
claimed_object: The squared-exponential covariance of the Gaussian-process exploration path.
actual_behaviour: A 1e-6 diagonal jitter is added to the covariance before the Cholesky factorisation, changing the sampled law from the intended GP to GP + 1e-6 white. Because the kernel is numerically the identity at the shipped length scale (see the white-noise finding), the jitter's whole effect is an amplitude rescaling of the noise by sqrt(1+1e-6).
fires_in_practice: MEASURED. The Cholesky diagonal is 1.000000500 at every shipped (dt, length_scale) tested, i.e. the jitter multiplies the exploration noise amplitude by 1.0000005 — a 5e-7 relative perturbation of a quantity (sigma = 0.1) that is itself a free exploration hyperparameter, so it cannot alter a reported number in any measurable way. The SVD fallback branch (line 432) is measured never to be taken; it does print a warning when taken, so that path is logged.
logged: The fallback path is logged ('Warning: Cholesky failed, using SVD for GP generation'); the jitter itself is not, which is acceptable for an inert clamp.
recommendation: Retain, and add the inertness comment the project rule requires: the jitter perturbs the amplitude of a free exploration hyperparameter by 5e-7 relative and cannot reach any reported quantity. Note that once the length scale is corrected (see the white-noise finding) the covariance will no longer be the identity and the jitter's role must be re-argued against the smallest eigenvalue of the corrected kernel.

name: 1e-12 / 1e-18 denominator epsilons in the reported cosine and R-squared metrics
location: src/solvers/continuous_oracle.py:94,95,103,104; run/study/h1h2_evaluation.py:379 (R-squared), 384 (cos), 428 (margin); run/study/mwe_e0_nn_critic.py:110,111,114; src/solvers/delayed_hopfield_pontryagin.py:168,169,174
claimed_object: The gradient-alignment cosine cos = <u_rep, u*>/(||u_rep|| ||u*||), the coefficient of determination, and the relative cost margin — all reported numbers, the cosine being the primary H2 diagnostic.
actual_behaviour: Each is computed as x/(y + eps) with eps in {1e-12, 1e-18}, so a division by an exactly-zero norm returns 0 instead of raising. When the denominator is a genuine O(1) norm the epsilon is a relative perturbation of order eps/||u*||; when the denominator is legitimately zero the metric silently reports a value (0, or a margin of 0) rather than declaring the quantity undefined.
fires_in_practice: MEASURED on the cell exercised (hopfield_linear, seed 0): the reported cosines are 0.857 / 0.999 / 0.942 and ||u*|| is O(1) (peak pre-clip max|u| = 2.495 over 2567 rollout steps), so the 1e-18 epsilon perturbs the cosine by order 1e-18 relative — beneath float64 resolution of the printed value. The degenerate case (a zero control norm, where the epsilon would silently manufacture cos = 0) is not observed on this cell and its rate is not measured on the other cells.
logged: No — acceptable for an inert epsilon, but none of the sites carries the comment stating why it is inert.
recommendation: Add the inertness comment at each site, naming the scale it is inert against (||u*|| is O(1) in every cell, so eps/||u*|| ~ 1e-18). Where the degenerate case is meaningful — a genuinely zero optimal control makes the alignment cosine undefined, not zero — raise or report 'not defined' rather than let the epsilon fabricate a 0 that a reader will average into a mean cosine.

name: Representation window over-spans the delay interval by three taps, and the configured window_size is silently discarded
location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:56-60 (`if not self.signature_conf.force_signature_window: self.signature_conf.window_size = self._compute_window_size()`; `return int(np.ceil(max_delay / self.env.step_size)) + 3 if max_delay > 0 else 10`)
claimed_object: The state of the delay differential equation is x_t : s -> x(t+s) for s in [-tau, 0]; its discretisation onto the control grid needs ceil(tau/dt) intervals, i.e. window_size = ceil(tau/dt) and window_size+1 samples spanning exactly tau.
actual_behaviour: Three extra taps are appended with no stated justification, so the window spans ceil(tau/dt)*dt + 3*dt > tau: the feature map is computed on a path strictly longer than the delay differential equation's state, mixing pre-history that the plant's evolution does not depend upon into the representation (and inflating the raw-history monomial dimension, which is the H2 fairness axis). Separately, the guard is inverted with respect to its documentation: conf/agent/value_gradient.yaml:51 says 'force_signature_window: if true, override window_size to match max delay', but the code overrides when the flag is FALSE — so the configured window_size is silently discarded on every shipped run, which sets the flag to false.
classification: D DISCRETISATION (the sampling is legitimate; the arithmetic over-spans tau, and the flag inversion means the configured value is not the one used)
fires_in_practice: MEASURED. env=delayed_oscillator_high_gap (tau=0.2, dt=0.05, conf/agent/value_gradient.yaml sets window_size: 40): the constructed agent reports window_size=7 against ceil(tau/dt)=4 — the configured 40 is discarded and three taps are added — giving a window span of 0.3500 s against tau = 0.2000 s, a ratio of 1.750. Same over-span measured on every cell probed: delayed_velocity_oscillator window_size=9 vs ceil(tau/dt)=6; hopfield_nonlinear 8 vs 5; MG_1D_limit_cycle 27 vs 24; MG_1D_chaotic 71 vs 68; delay_jax_unstable 13 vs 10. The inverted flag is already recorded in the repository's own documents/methodology/code_review.md:181-187 as finding F-H1.
logged: No. The constructed window is not printed against the configured one, so a study that sweeps agent.signature.window_size measures nothing.
recommendation: Derive the window as exactly ceil(tau/dt) taps (window_size+1 = ceil(tau/dt)+1 samples spanning tau, the smallest grid containing [-tau,0]), or state and justify the three extra taps if they are intended as an interpolation stencil margin — the number 3 appears nowhere in the mathematics and the sibling agent uses 1 for the same object. Fix the inverted guard, and log the resolved window_size, its span and the ratio span/tau in the run context so the discretisation of the state is auditable from the log alone. Note the fix must be coordinated with the parallel workflow, which owns src/agents/signatures_jax.py.
